    "text": "\r\n1.      Terms used in this document\r\nGeneral Terminology\r\n·       UUKPF: Unilever UK Pension Fund\r\n·       DB: Defined Benefit\r\n·       CARE: Career Average Revalued Earnings\r\n·       DC: Defined Contribution\r\n·       DCIP: DC Investing Plan\r\n·       EVC: Extra Voluntary Contributions: Additional contributions that can be made by the member either through a regular deduction in pay or as a one off. Contributions are invested in the Investing Plan.\r\n·       Legacy AVC: Historic Additional Voluntary Contributions held with Zurich, Equitable Life, Legal and General or Santander\r\n·       Hybrid: building up DB benefits and DC benefits at the same time. The DC will either be legacy AVCs or in the DC Investing plan.\r\n·       RSP: Retirement Savings Plan\r\n·       UFPLS: Uncrystallised Funds Pension Lump Sum\r\n·       PCLS: Pension Commencement Lump Sum\r\n·       GMP: Guaranteed Minimum Pension\r\n·       CETV: Cash Equivalent Transfer Value\r\n·       Relevant Employment: continuous period of employment whilst eligible for UUKPF membership whether or not membership chosen. Excludes employment for Unilever such as when on U-work contract or when on an International Assignment and not eligible for the UUKPF etc.\r\n·       Leave: leave Relevant Employment, may still be in Unilever employment such as on an International Assignment or U-work, or may have left Unilever\r\n·       NRD: Normal Retirement Date\r\n·       NRA: Normal Retirement Age\r\n·       SMPI: Statutory Money Purchase Illustration\r\n·       PAYE: Pay As You Earn\r\n·       LTA: Lifetime Allowance\r\n\r\nMember Categories:\r\nAny category not mentioned below will be linked to the DB section of the UUKPF. You can hover over the category on Hartlink which will provide a brief description.\r\n\r\n·       DCIP: Category for members building up DC Only benefits in the DCIP. Even though these members are only accruing DC benefits, these will be treated as a top up to DB benefits and will be linked to an opt out DB record.\r\nThere will also be DCIP records for members who elect to take an UFPLS at retirement. You will be able to identify these by checking the member’s record for a P event followed by a W event the day after, and an MTSIDDPA case on record.\r\n·       DC: Category for members building up DC Only benefits in the RSP. Treated as a ‘pure DC’ member        \r\n·       EDEF: Member who has opted out but still works for Unilever\r\n·       LAO: Life Assurance Only member (member who is not a member of a pension fund but is entitled to a death in service multiplier due to working for Unilever)\r\n\r\nFurther information can be found on the Journey of a Member Record Work Instruction &lt;https://capita.sharepoint.com/:w:/r/sites/capitaveritas/_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7B4FF60319-CF3C-44E7-9711-27339A40F289%7D&amp;file=Journey%20of%20a%20Member%20Record%20Post%20September%202021%20final%20(002).doc&amp;action=default&amp;mobileredirect=true&gt;\r\n\r\nMember Statuses\r\n·       Status A: Active Member contributing to the fund\r\n·       Status D: Deferred Member with Preserved Benefits\r\n·       Status P: Pensioner Member in receipt of an annual pension\r\n·       Status N: Life Assurance only/Non-Member\r\n·       Status W: Leaver: No Liability\r\n·       Status T: Transferred benefits out of the fund/no liability\r\n·       Status X: Deceased Member\r\n\r\nAnnual Renewal Key dates:\r\n\r\n2022\r\nAnnual Renewal Communications issued: wc 27/06/2022\r\nBenefit Statements issued: 28/06/2022\r\nAnnual Renewal Window Opens: 04/07/2022\r\nAnnual Renewal Window Closes: 12/08/2022 5pm\r\n\r\n\r\n2.      Membership - Joining the Fund, Leaving the Fund and Contributions\r\n2.1     How do I join the fund?\r\nThe DB section of the UUKPF closed to new members on 30 September 2021. New employees are now automatically enrolled into the Retirement Savings Plan (RSP) which is administered by Fidelity.\r\n\r\nMembers who opted out of the UUKPF on 30 September 2021 will be given the opportunity to opt back into the Fund once during the next two annual election windows (normally around July/August with changes taking effect from 1 October).\r\n\r\nPlease note that current members of the UUKPF can opt out of DB and enrol in the Defined Contribution Investing Plan (DCIP) within the same employment period.\r\n\r\n2.2     I recently joined the Company and Pension Fund but have not received a new joiner pack?\r\nDid the member join the Company after 30 September 2021?\r\n\r\nYES: They are a member of the Retirement Savings Plan. Request that they contact Fidelity\r\nNO: If the member has opted back into the Fund during an election window, tell them that Capita will issue a new joiner pack when they are notified by Unilever accordingly.\r\n\r\n2.3     How much do I contribute?\r\nYour contributions are 5% of your pensionable earnings up to the upper limit. As of 1 October 2021, this is £45,000 and will increase annually in line with inflation.\r\n\r\nYou can add to your benefits with Extra Voluntary Contributions (EVCs) into the DC Investing Plan. These can be regular or one-off payments.\r\n\r\n2.4     What is the Benefits Envelope?\r\nThe Benefits Envelope is an amount of money, calculated at 25% of your gross pensionable earnings.\r\n\r\nIt can be used to:\r\n-       Build up future benefits in the DB CARE plan (if eligible)\r\n-       Use for savings into the DCIP\r\n-       Use for additional taxable take-home pay.\r\n\r\nYou can decide what to do with your Benefits Envelope each year during the annual election window.\r\n\r\n2.5     Can I make additional contributions and how?\r\nYou can pay extra voluntary contributions to an Investing plan account in order to build up additional pension for your retirement. You can pay them on a regular basis or as occasional ‘one-off’ payment to your account.   \r\n\r\nYou can download a form to complete and return to the Pension team from the ‘downloadable documents’ on the UUKPF website www.uukpf.co.uk &lt;http://www.uukpf.co.uk&gt; . Once we have received the form we will make arrangements with payroll for deductions to commence.\r\n\r\nMembers can also elect to pay voluntary contributions during the annual election window to increase their Life Assurance Multiplier (for death in service), or top up their serious ill health benefits.\r\n\r\n2.6     Will I receive tax relief on my contributions?\r\nTax relief applies to your contributions at your highest rate of tax as per the table below:\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\nContributions are typically deducted from your salary using the Unilever Contribution Arrangement (also known as a salary sacrifice arrangement). Under the Unilever Contribution Arrangement, you will also benefit from National Insurance contribution savings in addition to the tax relief quoted above\r\n\r\n2.7     I have just checked my pension account and my contributions/balance are much less than I have contributed - why?\r\nIs the member looking at their Fidelity Investing Plan or a Statutory Money Purchase Illustration (SMPI) statement?\r\nYES: Tell the member this is in relation to their DC benefits only and these will fluctuate on a daily basis in line with their chosen investment.\r\n\r\nIf the member is looking at a recent benefit statement or annual renewal statement, remind them that their contributions and their employers’ go towards funding their pension accrual in the CARE Plan and the figure on their statement is an annual pension payable for life, it’s not a pot of money used to purchase a pension at retirement.\r\n\r\n2.8     What is the limit on how long I can contribute to the Fund?\r\nYou will normally contribute towards benefits in the Career average plan for up to 40 years. When you reach 40 years’ pensionable service, you have the option to continue contributions and build up further benefits for up to 45 years. Hence your ‘maximum pensionable service’ will be 40 years, or if you have reached 40 years it will be 40 or 45 years, depending on the choice you made on reaching 40 years.\r\n\r\nIf you work part time, your pensionable service is adjusted downwards to take account of the part time hours you actually worked.\r\n\r\n2.9     Can I transfer in benefits from other pension schemes?\r\nIf you have benefits in another registered pension arrangement, you may be able to transfer them into the Investing plan, as long as Unilever and the Trustees agree and the benefits do not include any ‘contracted-out’ benefits. Transfers in are now managed by Fidelity and when Capita receive an initial request for a transfer in, they will be forwarded as appropriate.\r\n\r\n2.10    Restrictions on transferring out within 6 months of NRA\r\nUnder their current discretionary policy, the Company and the Trustees have agreed that you must apply to transfer at least 6 months before your normal retirement age, all the transfer requirements must be completed and the transfer paid before normal retirement age.\r\n\r\nThis current policy gives you more time than your statutory right which requires you to apply and confirm the decision to transfer more than a year before your Normal Pension Age (other conditions apply as well).\r\n\r\n2.11    Can I opt out of the scheme?\r\nYes, you can opt out of the plan at any time. You can download a copy of the opt out form to complete at uukpf.co.uk.\r\n\r\nPlease note that, once opted out, you will only have one chance to opt back into the DB section of the Fund either in the next or following election window.\r\n\r\n2.12    What happens if I leave the scheme? Can I have my contributions back?\r\nIf you have two or more years’ pensionable service, are aged 55 or over, have a transfer in of benefits or another record with liability\r\n\r\nIf you leave the Fund and have two or more years’ pensionable service, you will become a deferred member. Your benefits will be calculated at the date you left the Fund and these will be effectively ‘frozen’ until you elect to take your benefits (from age 55). Your benefits will receive annual increases in deferment until you retire or elect to transfer out.\r\n\r\nYour Investing plan account will continue to be invested in line with your Fund choices. You cannot make any further contributions to your account. However, you can still make changes to your fund choices if you wish and should refer to the Investing Plan booklet for further information.\r\n\r\nIf you are over age 55, you will have the opportunity to retire directly from active service, provided that you have left relevant employment.\r\n\r\nIf you have less than two years’ pensionable service and not subject to the criteria above\r\n\r\nRefund of contributions\r\n\r\nYou can elect to receive a refund of your contributions plus interest, plus any Investing Plan contributions plus investment growth, less tax. This does not include any extra life cover contributions made by you or employer contributions.\r\n\r\nIf you made contributions through the Unilever Contribution Arrangement (UCA), the refund will be paid by Unilever to the bank account your salary was paid into. If not, Capita will pay the refund directly to you.\r\n\r\nIf you are over age 55, have previously transferred in benefits from another scheme or have another record in respect of service with Unilever which still contains liability, you are not entitled to a refund of contributions - even if you leave with less than two years’ pensionable service.\r\n\r\nDeferring your pension\r\nYou can elect to defer your benefits in line with the procedure detailed above for over two year leavers..     \r\n\r\nTransferring your pension\r\nYou can also choose to transfer all your Career average plan benefits and your Investing plan account into another arrangement.\r\n\r\nIf we do not receive a reply from you within 4 months of issuing your leaving service options, please note that the default option is an automatic refund of contributions.\r\n\r\n2.13    How does my pension increase in deferment?\r\n-       Benefits accrued before 1 July 2012: In line with January RPI up to a maximum of 5%\r\n-       Benefits accrued between 1 July 2012 and 30 September 2021: by the lower of:\r\no       The amount of RPI inflation over the whole period\r\no       2.5% for each year for the whole period.\r\n-       Benefits accrued from 1 October 2021: by the lower of:\r\no       The amount of CPI inflation over the whole period\r\no       2.5% for each year for the whole period.\r\n\r\nIf you leave due to redundancy, company sale or outsourcing, the CARE element of your pension may be increased in the same way as if you were still in pensionable service ie. broadly increased each year in line with inflation up to 5%\r\n\r\n2.14    What happens if I work part-time?\r\nIf you work part time, your contributions are adjusted to reflect this. They are still based on your pensionable earnings, but the lower and higher levels are reduced in line with the number of hours you actually work compared with ‘full-time’ hours.\r\n\r\n2.15    What happens to my contributions if I am on maternity/paternity leave?\r\nPaid leave\r\nDuring paid maternity, paternity, adoption or parental leave, you will pay contributions on the pay you receive and your pension will continue building up as normal based on your pensionable earnings at the date you went on leave.\r\n\r\nUnpaid leave\r\nDuring unpaid maternity, paternity, adoption or parental leave, your contributions will stop and you will normally stop building up pension benefits. On your return to work, you then have a one-off choice to buyback your missing pension. If you choose not to do this, you will not have pension benefits relating to that period. You will be told the cost of buying back this pension at the time.\r\n\r\nIf you elect to buyback you can pay this monthly over a maximum 6 month period or pay as a one-off payment from your salary.\r\n\r\nIf you die\r\nIf you die while you are on maternity, paternity, adoption or parental leave, the same type of benefits are payable as for death in pensionable service, whether the leave is paid or unpaid. If you die while on unpaid leave, the life cover lump sum and the pension you could have built up from the date you died to age 65 will generally be based on your pensionable earnings at the date you went on leave.\r\n\r\n2.16    What happens to my contributions if I am absent from work due to illness?\r\nPaid sick leave\r\nDuring paid sick leave, your pension will build up based on the pay you actually receive during the period of absence.\r\n\r\nUnpaid sick leave\r\nDuring unpaid sick leave, your contributions will stop and you will stop building up pension. There is no facility to make up contributions when you return to work.\r\n\r\nIf you die\r\nIf you die while you are on sick leave, the same type of benefits are payable as for death in pensionable service, whether the leave is paid or unpaid. If you die while on unpaid leave, the life cover lump sum and the pension you could have built up from the date you died to age 65 will generally be based on your pensionable earnings at the date you went on leave.\r\n\r\n2.17    What do I do if I think my service record is incorrect?\r\nThe Pension Fund is advised of your Company and Pensionable start date by the Company. If you joined a Unilever Company before 1988, you were unable to join the Fund until age 21. This reduced to age 18 from 6 April 1988. Some Unilever Companies also had a 6 month waiting period. (If the member advises they joined later than these dates, the Pensions Team need to look at the pension record more closely to confirm the position regarding service dates).\r\n\r\n2.18    International Assignees (IAs) - localising in the UK - am I in the Pension Fund/Why was I not enrolled when I localised?\r\nEmployees may come to the UK on an international assignment, which means they join the UK payroll and pay NI Contributions but stay in their home country pension fund. Some IAs do not return to their home country and remain in the UK and are ‘localised’, this means all their assignment allowances are stopped and any contributions to their home pension fund cease and they are treated the same as any other locally recruited UK employee.      \r\n\r\nIAs who localise after 30 September 2021 and have not opted out of the UUKPF previously should be enrolled into the RSP and queries forwarded to Fidelity as appropriate.\r\n\r\n2.19    I am transferring overseas, what will happen to my pension?\r\nAre you going on an International Assignment and are expected to return to the UK?\r\nYes: Provide EAT email details and advise EAT can confirm pension arrangements following transfer overseas on assignment.\r\n\r\nIf answer is NO and they are moving on a ‘permanent transfer’, they will be treated in the same way as a voluntary leaver.\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n3.      Death Benefits\r\n3.1     What provision will Unilever make for my spouse/civil partner if I die?\r\nA pension will be payable to a legally married spouse or civil partner.\r\n\r\nIf you have been married or in a civil partnership less than six months before your death, a pension is only payable at Trustees’ discretion.\r\n\r\nA pension may be payable to a dependant at the Trustees’ discretion. You can complete a dependant partner nomination form to nominate someone to receive a pension upon your death. This form can be downloaded from uukpf.co.uk.\r\n\r\nIf in service:\r\n\r\nHalf the pension you have built up to the date you died, plus if you die before age 65, half the pension you could have built up in the plan from the date you died to age 65 (up to your maximum pensionable service) based on your pensionable earnings at the date of death up to the upper limit.\r\n\r\nIf deferred:\r\n\r\nHalf your deferred pension, including increases up to the date you died.\r\n\r\nIf you left before 06/04/1997, your automatic lump sum will be converted into a pension and this will also be payable to your spouse/civil partner.\r\n\r\nIf retired:\r\n\r\nHalf the pension you were receiving at the date you died (ignoring any reduction from taking a cash sum).      \r\n\r\nThe pension will be adjusted if your spouse/civil partner is more than 10 years older or younger than you.     \r\n\r\n3.2     Can you tell me what the current value of the spouses’ pension is?\r\nWe should not provide this amount over the phone due to potential errors in quoting due to multiple benefit lines/inaccuracies in records. Open a case for the team to investigate.\r\n\r\n3.3     Can I increase the amount of pension payable to my spouse/civil partner?\r\nBefore you retire, you may be able to choose to start with a smaller pension for you and increase the amount payable to your spouse or civil partner after you die (up to a certain maximum). If you wish to investigate this option, please confirm your spouse/civil partner’s date of birth and we will refer to the actuary for calculation.\r\n\r\n3.4     What provision will Unilever make for my children if I die?\r\nPensions are payable to eligible children up to age 18 (or 23 if they are in full-time education) in the event of your death.\r\n\r\nChildren’s pensions are worked out as a percentage of your pension, which depends on whether or not a pension is also payable to your husband, wife, civil partner or other adult dependant, and how many children are entitled to receive benefits. The table below shows the total children’s pension payable in each situation (as a percentage of your pension) which will then be shared equally among the eligible children:\r\n\r\nNumber of Children      1       2       3       4 or more\r\nIf a spouses/civil partner pension paid 20%     30%     40%     50%\r\nIf no other pension is paid     30%     45%     60%     75%\r\n\r\nA child’s pension stops when the child reaches age 18 or 23 if they are still in full-time education. If a child is severely disabled, the Trustees may decide to pay them a pension for life.\r\n\r\n3.5     How do you determine who is eligible for a dependant’s pension?\r\nUpon your death, Capita will issue the informant with a beneficiary information form to identify any potential beneficiaries.\r\n\r\nAny dependant pension applications should be declared, and relevant evidence of financial dependency provided. \r\n\r\nIf there is a completed dependant partner nomination form on record in the name of the applicant and the Trustees have accepted this previously, we will put the pension into payment.\r\n\r\nIf there is no form on record, we will forward the information provided to the Trustees for them to assess the applicant’s eligibility for a pension.\r\n\r\n3.6     Is there a lump sum payment upon death?\r\nIf in service:\r\n\r\nA cash sum of:\r\no       Four times your pensionable earnings, ignoring the upper limit, at the date you die.  This is payable as long as you are a Unilever employee, you do not have to be building up benefits in a pension fund\r\no       Any extra life cover you have arranged from the plan\r\no       A refund of member contributions, with interest. This does not include any contributions towards extra life cover, serious ill health cover or from your Benefits Envelope paid by Unilever\r\no       The value of your Investing plan account would normally be payable as a cash sum.\r\n\r\nIf deferred:\r\n\r\no       A refund of member contributions, with interest\r\no       The value of your Investing plan account will normally be payable as a cash sum.\r\n\r\nIf retired:\r\n\r\nIf you die within five years of retiring, the balance of your pension for the rest of that five-year period, based on the monthly rate of pension you are receiving at the date of your death, will be payable as a cash sum. \r\n\r\nPLEASE NOTE: GMP and EPB only members do not have a Lump Sum payment payable upon death.\r\n\r\n3.7     How do I nominate somebody to receive a cash lump sum upon my death?\r\nYou will need to complete a nomination form to guide the Trustees about who should receive any cash sum benefit if you die. The form has two sections.\r\n\r\nSection A - you provide the names of close family only. The Trustees will be legally obliged to follow your instructions in this section, unless:\r\n\r\n-       the person you have nominated dies before you, or less than 28 days after you;\r\n-       you were single or not in a civil partnership when you made the nomination and have married or entered a civil partnership since (unless you have told us that your new status should not affect your nomination); or \r\n-       your nomination only covers part of the cash sum.\r\n\r\nSection B - you can name anyone in this section. The Trustees do not have to follow your instructions, but they will take them into account. If your instructions in this nomination in Section A does not apply, the Trustees will decide how to pay the cash sum. Please note: although the Trustees would normally expect to follow your wishes in Section B, they are not legally obliged to do so if Section A does not apply.\r\n\r\nPlease remember to keep your nomination form up to date. If your personal situation changes and you need to fill in a new form, please contact us so that we can issue this. Alternatively, you can download a blank form from www.uukpf.co.uk &lt;http://www.uukpf.co.uk&gt;.\r\n\r\n3.8     Can I pay for extra life cover?\r\nWhen you first join the plan, you can choose to pay more into the plan towards extra cover, up to a total of eight times your pensionable earnings (You have to choose a whole multiple). You will be sent a form and the current rates for the different levels of cover when you join the plan. You will then have the opportunity to change your level of life cover once a year, in October, but you may need to confirm you are in good health if you wish to increase your level of life cover after joining. The option to buy extra life cover is subject to Unilever’s consent and Unilever can withdraw the option at any time.\r\n\r\n3.9     When a member dies is a P45 sent out?\r\nYes - when a member dies a P45 is sent to the tax office by Capita, this is only done when all monies have been settled/paid.\r\n\r\n3.10    When a member dies is a P60 sent out?\r\nNo - The P60 details are not automatically sent out.   This can be requested by family or executor and a case needs to be raised under MTSCOEPA and a certificate of earnings letter is sent out.\r\n\r\n\r\n4.       Benefits\r\n\r\n4.1     What is the accrual rate of my pension?\r\nFrom 1 October 2021, the accrual rate for future CARE pension entitlement is 1/80.\r\n\r\n4.2     How is my pension calculated?\r\nCareer Average Plan\r\n\r\nYou earn a yearly pension of 1/80 of your pensionable earnings up to the upper limit for each year of pensionable service (adjusted as appropriate if you join or leave part way through a year). This yearly amount then increases each year in line with inflation up to a maximum of 5% until you leave pensionable service.\r\n\r\nYour total CARE pension on leaving the scheme is each years’ accrued pension (plus increases) added together.  \r\n\r\nFinal Salary Plan\r\n\r\nThe higher of:\r\n\r\n(1) 1/60 of your final pensionable salary at date of leaving multiplied by your pensionable service up to 30 June 2012 (calculated in years and months)\r\n\r\n(2) Your Final Salary Pension calculated at 30 June 2012 (using the methodology calculated above) with pension increases applied to date of leaving.\r\n\r\nThis is a high level overview of how a member’s DB pension is calculated and a case should be opened for a full breakdown/further clarification if requested.\r\n\r\n4.3     Can I have a Quote/Estimate of my pension?\r\nYes! Log cases on Hartlink depending on the member’s request:\r\n\r\nMTSQUOTE - used for simple quotes that run through the system\r\nMTSQUOTM - used for quotes that require a manual calculation (eg. Diversey)\r\nMTSQUOTC - used for complex quotes that require calculation by SCT (eg. Birdseye/Bestfoods)\r\nMTSPBUP - current value of deferred benefits and a good indicator of benefits at NRD. It is preferable to use this case over a quote if the member is not close to retirement age.\r\nComplete the MET Checklist &lt;https://capita.sharepoint.com/:x:/r/sites/capitaveritas/Shared%20Documents/MET%20Checklist%20v3%20NEW.xlsx?d=w60727c7a9f844f2f8d56133f80629d5b&amp;csf=1&amp;web=1&amp;e=qaMEL6&gt; to determine which quote case type to open. If still unsure open  a MTSENQAC and Triage will conduct a full investigation and open the relevant case the same working day.\r\n\r\nPlease note: we should only offer the member a maximum of 3 quotes and there is little point doing quotes for retirement dates quite close to each other (eg. doing quotes for both May and June 2022).\r\n\r\n4.4     Can I transfer my pension out of the Fund?\r\nAs long as you are a deferred member, you can request to transfer all or part of your benefits out of the Fund up to 6 months before your NPA, with transfers completed and paid before you actually reach NPA.\r\n\r\nIf you want a Cash Equivalent Transfer Value (CETV) and discharge forms, please contact Capita. You are entitled to one free CETV in a 12 month period, any subsequent requests are subject to a charge of £78 plus VAT.      \r\n\r\nPlease note that if your transfer contains DB benefits and the value is over £30,000, then you will be required to seek Financial Advice and provide a statement from an FCA regulated adviser before a transfer of benefits can proceed.\r\n\r\nDB transfers are guaranteed for 3 months.\r\n\r\n4.5     What Is Stronger Nudge?\r\nFrom 1 June 2022, Pension Schemes that provide ‘flexible’ benefits (ie. DC benefits) are required to give members a ‘Stronger Nudge’ towards pension guidance delivered by PensionWise before they access or transfer your benefits.\r\n\r\nIf any of your benefits contains a DC element (for example, the Investing Plan), you will be affected.\r\n\r\nAt the point of accessing or transferring your benefits, you will either be required to take the guidance from PensionWise, opt out or declare that you are exempt accordingly.\r\n\r\nIf you wish to take PensionWise guidance, you can either book the appointment, or Capita can do this on your behalf. Your retirement or transfer request will then be placed on hold until the appointment has taken place.   \r\n\r\n4.6     Am I exempt from Stronger Nudge?\r\nThe following transactions are exempt from Stronger Nudge:\r\n\r\nTransfer Cases:\r\n-       The member is under age 50 (because the service is only available for people 50 and over)\r\n-       The purpose is not to receive flexible benefits as a result of the transfer\r\n-       The member has already been referred to guidance by another scheme (regardless of whether the member took up the offer or opted out)\r\n-       The transfer is from an occupational scheme to a personal pension scheme regulated by the FCA; these are exempt from the nudge; in this case, the receiving personal pension provider would, instead, be responsible for making the nudge.\r\n-       where a personal pension provider has already provided the member with retirement risk warnings, and the scheme believes that the member’s circumstances haven’t changed significantly to require a further warning   \r\n\r\nRetirement Cases:\r\n-       if they have received Pension Wise guidance in the last 12 months\r\n-       if they have received regulated financial advice in the last 12 months\r\nThe member will need to indicate this within their Retirement Option Form.\r\n\r\n4.7     I’ve returned my transfer discharge forms - what next?\r\nTransferring your pension can, sometimes, be a lengthy process. Even once paperwork is complete, there are multiple reasons why there could be hold ups in the process and some of the most common ones are noted below:      \r\n\r\n-       Due diligence checks - the Trustees are currently conducting enhanced due diligence checks due to changes in Pension Transfer Regulations on 30 November 2021 and we may write to you requesting further information (please refer to the FAQ &lt;https://capita.sharepoint.com/:w:/r/sites/capitaveritas/_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7BE77496A0-382D-41EF-B651-37C5AFC72E44%7D&amp;file=New%20Transfer%20Rules%20-%20FAQs%20(MET).docx&amp;action=default&amp;mobileredirect=true&gt; if the member has any questions about the post 30/11 transfer process)\r\n-       Awaiting dealing dates for disinvestment of DC funds.\r\n\r\nUnder legislation Capita have 6 months from the guarantee date (the calculation date) of the CETV to pay the transfer. If the transfer application is comprised solely of DC benefits, we have 6 months from the date the transfer documentation was returned.\r\n\r\n4.8     What is GMP?\r\nUntil 6 April 2016, the Fund was 'contracted out' of the State Second Pension.\r\n\r\nIf you have pensionable service between 6 April 1978 and 5 April 1997, you paid a lower rate of National Insurance contributions, and in return, the UUKPF will to provide you with a level of benefits equivalent to what you would had received from the State Earnings Related Pension Scheme (the SERPS) had the fund not been contracted out.\r\n\r\nOnce you reach your 'GMP age' - which is 65 for men and 60 for women - the GMP part of your pension take effect and receives different increases - see 5.9. If you are the husband, wife or civil partner of a member and you're receiving a pension with GMP (a widow’s(er’s) GMP), this different increase will apply whatever your age.   \r\n\r\n4.9     Is the Fund equalised?\r\nBenefits in the Fund are equalised with the exception of GMP. In relation to GMP equalisation, the Trustees are currently discussing this, however there is no timescale for an update.\r\n\r\n5.      Retirement\r\n\r\n5.1     What is my NPA/NRD?\r\nTypically this is age 65. However there are exceptions below:\r\n-       Some members have a ‘True NRA’ of age 60 (eg. female GMPONLY members)\r\n-       Some members have benefits that are payable unreduced from age 60 although their NRA is still age 65 under the Trust Deed and Rules\r\n-       Active members and EDEF members still in relevant employment can retire after age 65 (ie. when employment ends)\r\n\r\n5.2     Can I retire early?\r\nThe earliest age you can currently retire from the Fund on a voluntary basis is age 55.\r\n\r\nIf you retire early, your pension will then be reduced for early payment - to take account of the expectation that you will receive it for longer than if you had started it your NPA. This reduction is currently 4.5% for each year you retire before NPA. If different tranches of pension benefit are payable unreduced at different dates, each tranche will be reduced by the relevant early retirement factor accordingly.\r\n\r\n5.3     Are there guidelines/criteria for Ill Health Retirement?\r\nMembers have to be over age 23 with 5+ years pensionable service and unfit to carry out their own occupation or have limited their earnings capacity. The case is referred to Occupational Health who then assess the member’s application.\r\n\r\n5.4     If I have to cease employment due to ill health can I take my pension?\r\nIf you have to stop working for Unilever and leave pensionable service because of serious ill health or permanent incapacity, you may be eligible to receive a pension provided you meet the criteria in 5.3. The serious ill-health pension is made up of:\r\n\r\n-       Your Career average plan pension, based on the years’ worth of pension you have built up to the time you retire, plus\r\n-       1/80th of your pensionable earnings (up to the upper limit) for each year you could have built up pension from the time you retire to age 65. The years of pension you have built up, plus these ‘extra’ years, are limited to your maximum pensionable service.\r\n\r\nFrom 1 October 2021, if your pensionable earnings are above the upper limit (currently £45,000), and you opted to pay for the voluntary serious ill health DC top up benefit, you may receive an additional payment from Unilever to your DCIP account. This must be used on retirement to buy additional benefits.\r\n\r\n5.5     Can a deferred member take pension early due to ill health?\r\nIf you wish to apply for ill health retirement from deferred status, please contact Capita. We will forward you a pack for you/your GP or consultant to complete. This will be then forward to Occupational Health and Unilever for them to assess your application.\r\n\r\nIf an application is approved, you will receive a pension (of which the final salary element is payable unreduced).\r\n\r\nNOTE: If your health improves, Unilever has the right to suspend or reduce any pension you are receiving.      \r\n\r\n5.6     What is the process for retirement?\r\nActive member:\r\n\r\nWe will receive confirmation from UniOps that you are leaving your Unilever employment and are retiring. Once we receive this notification we will issue you with a retirement pack which will contain your retirement options and forms for you to complete.\r\n\r\nDeferred member:\r\n\r\nWe will write to you approximately 13 months before your NRD with a retirement pack which will contain your retirement options and forms of you to complete. Alternatively you can contact us anytime after age 55 requesting a retirement pack.\r\n\r\nSo we can ensure your benefits are paid in a timely manner, please remember to keep Capita updated to any changes to your contact details.\r\n\r\nIf you do not claim your benefits at NRD in a timely manner, the same level of pension as would have been payable at NRD will be paid at actual retirement and arrears will be paid for the period not received. There are however restrictions to the number of years of arrears of backdated pay that may be made (6 years, any more is payable at Trustees’ discretion), and there is normally no interest for late payment.\r\n\r\nPaying your benefits once forms have been returned\r\nAccessing your pension can, sometimes, be a lengthy process. Even once the paperwork is complete, there are multiple reasons why there could be hold ups in the process and some of the most common ones are noted below:     \r\n\r\n·       Missing information or data mismatches\r\n·       A transfer of benefits selected\r\n·       Open Market Option\r\n·       Awaiting payment of final contributions (active members only)\r\n·       Awaiting disinvestment of Investing Plan/AVC funds.\r\n\r\n5.7     Can I take a lump sum?\r\nThere are multiple ways you may be able to take a lump sum at retirement:\r\n\r\n·       Via a tax free Pension Commencement Lump Sum (PCLS) - normally payable by exchanging some of your annual pension for tax free cash, up to a maximum of 25% of your total benefits [NOTE TO ADMIN: there are exceptions to this (eg. the member’s pension is restricted due to GMP, GMPONLY members cannot commute ANY pension into a PCLS)]\r\n·       If you have DC benefits, you can elect to take these as a Uncrystallised Pension Funds Lump Sum (UFPLS). 25% of this will be payable tax free and the remainder is taxable through PAYE.\r\n·       Via a Trivial Commutation Lump Sum/Small Lump Sum (see 5.8)\r\n\r\nOther providers may be able to offer other options in addition to the above (eg. via Flexible Access Drawdown) and Capita recommend you seek Financial Advice before making a decision.\r\n\r\n5.8     Can I take my whole fund as a one off lump sum?\r\nMembers with sufficiently small benefits may be able to take the entirety of their benefits as a lump sum.     \r\n\r\nIf the HMRC valuation of your benefits in the UUKPF and elsewhere do not exceed £30,000, you may be eligible to take a Trivial Commutation Lump Sum.\r\nIf the value of the Lump Sum payable (ie. your CETV) does not exceed £10,000, this is classed as a small lump sum. These are payable regardless of benefits in payment from other schemes.\r\n\r\nCurrently, members with Post 17/05/1990 GMP can not take a Trivial Commutation/Small Lump Sum.\r\n\r\nNOTE TO ADMIN: It is important that you do not state whether a member is definitely eligible for Trivial Commutation - open a case for the team to investigate.\r\n\r\n5.9     Once my pension is in payment will it increase?\r\nOnce in payment, your pension increases on 1 April each year. Parts of your pension may receive different increases:\r\n\r\nPension built up before 1 January 2008: In line with January RPI, capped at 5%\r\nPension built up from 1 January 2008 - 30 June 2012: In line with January RPI, capped at 3%/5% (if paid higher rate contributions)\r\nPension built up from 1 July 2012 - 30 September 2021: In line with January RPI, capped at 3%/5% (if paid higher rate contributions)\r\nPension built up from 1 October 2021: In line with January CPI, capped at 3%\r\n\r\nIf you are at/over GMP age, the GMP element of your pension will increase as follows:\r\n\r\nPre 88 GMP receives no increases from the fund\r\nPost 88 GMP receives statutory increases (ie. September CPI capped at 3%)\r\n\r\nFor benefits from 1 January 2008 - 30 September 2021, members had the option of paying higher rate contributions to receive a higher cap on their pension increase. You can tell the cap by looking at the last number on the benefit line - does it end with 3 or 5 (eg. UCAR123 is standard rate, UCAR125 is higher rate)?\r\n\r\n5.10    What is the level pension option? Can I get a level pension quote?\r\nThe Level Pension Option can be investigated for all members with Final Salary benefits. If you wish to receive details of the Level Pension Option, simply ask for this when requesting a quote or retirement pack.\r\n\r\nBy taking the Level Pension Option, you will receive a higher amount of pension when you retire, up to the Basic State Pension amount. When you reach State Pension Age (currently age 66+), your UUKPF will then decease when you start receiving your State Pension, effectively resulting in the overall amount of benefit you receive to be constant (ie. ‘levelled out’).\r\n\r\n5.1     Will my pension decrease when I reach State Pension Age?\r\nIf member took the Level Pension Option at retirement, the ‘temporary’ pension element of their pension will cease. This can be checked by viewing a temporary benefit line (most benefit lines will have the word TEMP in them but ask if you are unsure) and checking for a cease date, as per the below example:\r\n\r\n\r\nAlternatively, the pension may have already ceased, as per the below:\r\n\r\nIf the member is within a month of their State Pension Age, or has passed their State Pension Age and the temporary pension has not been ceased open a MTSBRIDG case so the benefits can be reduced accordingly.\r\nTo check the member’s State Pension Age click here &lt;https://www.gov.uk/state-pension-age&gt;.\r\n\r\n5.2     Can I take part of my DC benefits as a lump sum and reinvest the rest?\r\nYes - but not with the UUKPF!\r\n\r\nAt retirement, you will have the option to take part of your benefits from the Fund, and transfer the remainder elsewhere, this can be either to an external provider or a Master Trust administered by Fidelity.\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n6.      Support for members\r\n6.1     Will I receive regular updates?\r\nActive members will receive a benefit statement annually.\r\nIn addition to this, members paying into the DCIP will receive an annual SMPI statement.\r\n\r\nPension schemes under legislation do not have to provide deferred members with an annual statement, however we will issue a Preserved Benefit Update upon request.\r\n\r\n6.2     Can I view my pension details online?\r\nThis is currently in development but cannot give a timescale as to when this will be completed. We will communicate to you when the online service is up and running.\r\n\r\n6.3     What support will be available for members?\r\nThe website uukpf.co.uk has lots of useful links and information for members so please direct them to this page in the first instance.\r\n\r\nPensioner members may also have joined their regional Unilever Pensioner Association (UPA) - see 10.1 for contact details should we receive any queries.\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n7.      Tax and Pay\r\n7.1     On what day of the month will I get paid?\r\nPensions are generally paid on or around the 7th or 21st of each month. If the 7th or 21st falls on a weekend or a bank holiday, your pension will be paid on the first working day before this.\r\n\r\nIn the interface tab it will show the member as UNILV07 if paid on the 7th of the month and UNILV21 if paid on the 21st of the month. You can also check the Pensioner Number on Hartlink; this will start with U07 or U21    \r\n\r\n\r\n\r\nNOTE: If the member has received an UFPLS payment check their UFPLS record for the corresponding payment date as this may be different to the pension!\r\n\r\n7.2     Will I get a payslip?\r\nYou will receive a payslip if your pension changes by more than £1 when compared to the previous month. The exceptions to this are the March payslip which will include P60 information and so will be issued to all members and the April payslip for those members whose pension is increased.\r\n\r\nA member can request that a payslip is sent every month. This can be done by adding a YESSLIP note to record.  \r\n\r\n7.3     Do I pay tax on my pension?\r\nPayment of a regular pension is subject to income tax and is therefore taxed as appropriate through PAYE.      \r\n\r\nPension Commencement Lump Sums are normally paid tax free.\r\n\r\nTrivial Commutation Lump Sums and UFPLS payments are payable at a rate of 25% tax free, 75% taxable through PAYE.\r\n\r\n7.4     What is the Annual Allowance (AA)?\r\nThe Annual Allowance is the yearly amount of tax efficient pension savings you can build up in registered pension schemes before a tax charge arises (the ‘annual allowance charge’).\r\n\r\nFrom 2014/15 onwards, the Annual Allowance is £40,000.\r\n\r\nIf you are an active member, you can request an Annual Allowance statement. Alternatively, if you are at risk of exceeding the Annual Allowance, Capita will automatically issue you with a statement no later than the 6th of October following the end of the relevant tax year.\r\n\r\nThere is also an Annual Allowance specifically for Money Purchase (DC) benefits which is triggered when benefits are flexibly accessed (eg. via an UFPLS). This is the Money Purchase Annual Allowance. From 2017/18 onwards, the Money Purchase Annual Allowance is £4,000. If this is triggered, you will be notified when UFPLS benefits are settled.\r\n\r\n7.5     What is the Lifetime Allowance (LTA)?\r\nThe lifetime allowance is the total amount of registered pension scheme benefits you can build up over your working life before a tax charge arises (the ‘Lifetime Allowance charge’). This includes benefits from all sources except the State Pension. The Lifetime Allowance is £1,073,100 and will remain at this level until April 2026.\r\n\r\nThe Lifetime Allowance has changed multiple times over the years, as per the below table.\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\nWhen you retire, you use up some of the Lifetime Allowance. It is therefore important that you keep track of your benefits against the allowance. At retirement, we will ask you for details of other pensions in payment so we can ensure payment of your benefits will not cause you to exceed the Lifetime Allowance - you can find percentages on relevant provider paperwork.\r\n\r\nThe Lifetime Allowance is calculated as follows:\r\n\r\nCalculate the ‘total benefit crystallised’\r\n-       20 x Annual Pension\r\n-       PLUS any PCLS\r\n-       PLUS and DC benefit taken\r\nCalculate the percentage:\r\n-       Divide the ‘total benefit crystallised’ by the Lifetime Allowance (currently £1,037,000)\r\n-       Multiply by 100.\r\n\r\nIf you are over the allowance when you retire, you will pay the Lifetime Allowance charge on the value of the benefits that exceed the Lifetime Allowance. The excess may be paid as pension or it may be possible for it to be drawn as a cash sum.\r\n\r\nMembers may ask for details of their Lifetime Allowance for pensions already in payment - open a case for the team to calculate this.\r\n\r\n7.6     Lifetime Allowance Protections\r\nOn 6th April 2016, the Standard Lifetime Allowance applicable to pension savings reduced from £1.25 million to £1 million. The government put measures in place (in the form of ‘LTA Protection’) to ensure higher earning members at the time were not severely impacted.\r\n\r\nIndividual Protection 2016 (IP2016)\r\nIP2016 is only available if the value of your pension savings on 5 April 2016 was over £1 million. IP2016 will give you a protected Lifetime Allowance equal to the value of your pension savings on 5 April 2016, subject to an overall maximum of £1.25 million.\r\n\r\nFixed Protection 2016 (FP2016)\r\nFP2016 is available to members with pension savings of any value provided they are not contributing.  FP2016 will give a member a personal lifetime allowance of £1.25 million. They must not have Enhanced Protection, Primary Protection, or any other form of Fixed Protection\r\n\r\nFP2016 can be lost if the lifetime allowance subsequently increases to more than the protected amounts.        \r\n\r\nYou can apply online for Individual/Fixed Protection at &lt;https://www.gov.uk/guidance/pension-schemes-protect-your-lifetime-allowance&gt;\r\n\r\n7.7     What is A-Day?\r\nA-Day is 6 April 2006 - it is the day the Government introduced major changes to personal and company pension rules.\r\n\r\n-       A new lifetime allowance was introduced, placing a limit on the amount an individual could hold in personal and company pension schemes without being taxed.\r\n-       Most personal pensions pay out a tax-free lump sum at retirement, and this was fixed at a maximum of 25%. There is transitional protection for those who would have had the right to a higher figure based on the rules that applied before 6 April 2006. Members of the Unilever UK Pension Fund are not subject to transitional protection.\r\n\r\n7.8     Can my pension be paid annually?\r\n\r\nYes - but this is only done on request and is not generally offered.\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n8.      Pensions on divorce\r\n8.1     What happens to my pension if I divorce?\r\nIf you get divorced or end a civil partnership, your former partner will lose any automatic right to a pension if you die. However, the courts may allocate some of your pension benefits to them as part of the settlement.  \r\n\r\nThe most common arrangement is transferring a specified percentage of your pension to a pension provider in your ex-spouse/civil partner’s name - this is known as a pension sharing order.\r\n\r\nNOTE: The process/requirements are different for divorce in Scotland/Northern Ireland, if applicable tell the member details will be sent on request.\r\n\r\nIf you have been separated from your husband, wife or civil partner for more than two years, you can be treated as unmarried or not in a civil partnership if you apply to the Trustees and the Trustees agree. You can then apply for a dependant’s pension for your new partner. If you were to die in this situation, your husband, wife or civil partner may still receive a reduced pension.\r\n\r\n8.2     Can you please send me a Cash Equivalent Transfer Value (CETV) for divorce purposes?\r\nYes! We are able to provide you with a CETV. You are entitled to one CETV free of charge in a 12 month period. Any additional requests for a CETV will be charged at £78+VAT.\r\n\r\nPlease note that if you are in receipt of a pension and over NPA, the CETV request is also chargeable at the above rate.\r\n\r\n8.3     Is there a charge for implementing a pension sharing order?\r\nThe administration charge for implementing a pension sharing order is £1,350+VAT. Who pays the administration charge is detailed out in the pension sharing annex (eg. by the member, ex-spouse/civil partner or split equally between both parties).\r\n\r\nIf applicable, the ex-spouse/civil partner can elect to have their proportion of charges deducted from their pension credit. The member can also have their charge deducted from their benefits, however this is an option not typically offered.\r\n\r\n8.4     How long does it take for a Pension Share to be implemented and when does the member ex-spouse receive any monies?\r\nOnce Capita receives all information required to implement the order (including charges), then Capita has 4 months under legislation to implement the order and organise for the transfer of the pension credit to be made. However, we will endeavour to implement the order quicker than this.\r\n\r\n8.5     What is the Pension Sharing Process?\r\n-       Capita receive pension sharing documentation\r\n-       Capita to review documents and respond to order with any required amendments and a request for ex-spouse/civil partner pension provider details within 21 calendar days - this is known as the postponement of implementation\r\n-       Capita to also issue requests for charges to relevant parties\r\n-       Once all information/charges received, Capita to issue notice of implementation to both parties within 21 calendar days\r\n-       Capita then have 4 months (the implementation period) from the date all information received to implement the order, during this time we will disinvest any required DC benefits, calculate and pay the pension credit due to the ex-spouse/civil partner’s pension provider and reduce the member’s benefits as appropriate.        \r\n-       Capita to issue a notice of discharge of liability to all parties within 21 calendar days - however this is typically done in the implementation period.\r\n\r\n\r\n9.      Redundancy\r\nIf a member is being made redundant and makes enquiries around making additional payments into the Unilever Pension make them aware that payments can only be made whist they are an active member of the scheme.\r\n\r\n9.1     How will you be notified I’m leaving, I’m being made redundant?\r\nYour line manager will advise UniOps of your leaving via the Workday system. This will trigger a notification to be sent to the Unilever UK Pension Fund administrators, Capita.\r\n\r\n9.2     Can I pay part of my severance lump sum into my pension?\r\nYes, this can be paid into the DCIP. This must be done before you leave service. You will need to speak to UniOps to do this. Doing this will also count towards your Pension Input Amount for your Annual Allowance.\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n10.     Miscellaneous\r\n10.1    Which internal chaser blocks route to Darlington Team 1 Tray?\r\nNON SLA Chaser Blocks                                  With SLA Chaser Blocks\r\n1st Chaser Block            MTSCHASD                                                       CHASDSLA            \r\n\r\n2nd Chaser Block           MTSCHSD2                                                       CHASDSL2\r\n3rd Chaser block            MTSCHSD1                                                       CHASDSL3\r\n\r\n10.2    Unilever Pensioner Association (UPA) Queries? Who do we refer these members to?\r\nThese queries will usually/mainly be from existing pensioners or individuals who have just retired.\r\nThey could be about any/all of the following:\r\n\r\n-       Am I eligible for membership of UPA?\r\n-       Pensioner Lunches / Lunch invitations\r\n-       Birthday cards and vouchers\r\n-       Regional group membership\r\n-       Visiting scheme\r\n-       Unilever Shares\r\n\r\nPlease refer the member to expertadminteam@unilever.com &lt;mailto:expertadminteam@unilever.com&gt; or send them an email on the member’s behalf.\r\n\r\nNo action is required by either the Darlington or Sheffield team to answer these queries.\r\n\r\n10.3    UNIAC members? Do we refer these members or deal with them?\r\nUNIAC benefits only:\r\nAsk caller to email: expertadminteam@unilever.com &lt;mailto:expertadminteam@unilever.com&gt; with their query.      \r\n\r\nUNIAC / UPF / other Unilever benefits:\r\nCapita to deal with the query as a whole, but if the member has a query on their UNIAC element of pension, Capita to contact EAT with this element of the query.\r\n\r\n10.4    Transfer of calls to other teams\r\nIf you require someone from the back office team to call a member/next of kin/third party, open a MTSCALLB and inform them that someone will call them within 48 hours.\r\n\r\n10.5    New Joiner calls\r\nMembers who join Unilever from 1 October 2021 will be automatically enrolled into the RSP and should be forwarded to Fidelity as appropriate, with the following exceptions:\r\n\r\n-       Expression of Wish requests for RSP members\r\n-       Death in Service for RSP/Life Assurance Only members.\r\n\r\nCapita should hold a skeleton record for RSP/Life Assurance Only members, therefore if we don’t have one and we receive a call regarding the above, we should liaise with EAT.\r\n\r\n10.6    Non Member Calls\r\nIf they do have any paperwork or documentation to show they were part of the Fund, ask them to send a copy of this to us for us to investigate further.\r\n\r\nThere could be reasons why there is no record for them. For instance they may have been too young to join the plan. This person for example looks to have only been 15 if they joined in 1972 so wouldn’t have been eligible to join the plan until reaching age 21.\r\nIf members took a refund or transferred then we should still hold a record for them on Hartlink, or have details of them on the historic transfer books.\r\n\r\nIf they have some evidence or know specific dates and company names etc. we can investigate further - open a MTSNONM on the dummy record 45447775.\r\n\r\n10.7    Certificates\r\nIf a member (or third party) is asked to provide certificates e.g. Birth Certificate, Marriage Certificate, these need to be originals.\r\n\r\nWe can also accept certified copies of Power of Attorney and Court of Protection documents however we will require the full document.\r\n\r\n10.8    PSTR, SCON &amp; ECON - Tax References\r\n\r\nPension Scheme Tax Reference - PSTR     00490486RW\r\nFormer Scheme Contracted Out Number - SCON      S2803927E\r\nFormer Employer&#96;s Contracting Out Number  - ECON        E3800727C\r\n\r\n10.9    HR Enquiries\r\nAll HR related enquiries should be forwarded to EAT under 11.     "original": "# Define Q&amp;A pairs from the FAQ - Batch 1: Membership\n$articles = @(\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - How do I join the pension fund?\"\n        content = \"The DB section of the UUKPF closed to new members on 30 September 2021. New employees are now automatically enrolled into the Retirement Savings Plan (RSP) which is administered by Fidelity.\n\nMembers who opted out of the UUKPF on 30 September 2021 will be given the opportunity to opt back into the Fund once during the next two annual election windows (normally around July/August with changes taking effect from 1 October).\n\nCurrent members of the UUKPF can opt out of DB and enrol in the Defined Contribution Investing Plan (DCIP) within the same employment period.\"\n        keywords = \"join,membership,UUKPF,pension,RSP,Fidelity,enrol\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - I haven't received my new joiner pack\"\n        content = \"If you joined the Company after 30 September 2021, you are a member of the Retirement Savings Plan (RSP). Please contact Fidelity for your joiner pack.\n\nIf you joined before 30 September 2021 and opted back into the Fund during an election window, Capita will issue a new joiner pack when notified by Unilever.\"\n        keywords = \"joiner pack,new member,RSP,Fidelity\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - How much do I contribute to the pension?\"\n        content = \"Your contributions are 5% of your pensionable earnings up to the upper limit. These can be regular or one-off payments.\"\n        keywords = \"contributions,5%,pensionable earnings,EVCs,voluntary\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - What is the Benefits Envelope?\"\n        content = \"The Benefits Envelope is an amount of money, calculated at 25% of your gross pensionable earnings.\n\nIt can be used to:\n- Build up future benefits in the DB CARE plan (if eligible)\n- Use for savings into the DCIP\n- Use for additional taxable take-home pay\n\nYou can decide what to do with your Benefits Envelope each year during the annual election window.\"\n        keywords = \"benefits envelope,25%,CARE,DCIP,election window\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Can I make additional contributions?\"\n        content = \"Yes, you can pay extra voluntary contributions to an Investing plan account in order to build up additional pension for your retirement.     "original": "# Batch 3: Leaving the scheme, part-time, maternity\n$articles = @(\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - What happens if I leave the pension scheme?\"\n        content = \"If you have two or more years pensionable service:\nYou will become a deferred member. Your benefits will be calculated at the date you left and effectively frozen until you elect to take them (from age 55). Benefits receive annual increases in deferment.\n\nYour Investing plan account continues to be invested. You cannot make further contributions but can still change fund choices.\n\nIf over age 55, you can retire directly from active service provided you have left relevant employment.\n\nIf you have less than two years pensionable service:\nYou can elect to receive a refund of your contributions plus interest, plus any Investing Plan contributions plus investment growth, less tax. This does not include extra life cover contributions or employer contributions.\n\nIf you made contributions through the Unilever Contribution Arrangement (UCA), the refund will be paid by Unilever to your bank account. Otherwise, Capita will pay the refund directly.\n\nNote: If over age 55, previously transferred in benefits, or have another record with liability, you are not entitled to a refund even with less than two years service.\n\nIf no reply received within 4 months, the default option is an automatic refund of contributions.\"\n        keywords = \"leave scheme,deferred,refund,contributions,leaving service\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - How does my pension increase in deferment?\"\n        content = \"Pension increases in deferment depend on when benefits were accrued:\n\nBenefits accrued before 1 July 2012: In line with January RPI up to a maximum of 5%\n\nBenefits accrued between 1 July 2012 and 30 September 2021: By the lower of:\n- The amount of RPI inflation over the whole period\n- 2.5% for each year for the whole period\n\nBenefits accrued from 1 October 2021: By the lower of:\n- The amount of CPI inflation over the whole period\n- 2.5% for each year for the whole period\n\nIf you leave due to redundancy, company sale or outsourcing, the CARE element of your pension may be increased in the same way as if you were still in pensionable service (broadly in line with inflation up to 5%).\"\n        keywords = \"deferment,increases,RPI,CPI,inflation,deferred pension\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - What happens if I work part-time?\"\n        content = \"If you work part time, your contributions are adjusted to reflect this. They are still based on your pensionable earnings, but the lower and higher levels are reduced in line with the number of hours you actually work compared with full-time hours.\"\n        keywords = \"part-time,contributions,hours,adjusted\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - What happens to my pension on maternity or paternity leave?\"\n        content = \"Paid leave:\nDuring paid maternity, paternity, adoption or parental leave, you will pay contributions on the pay you receive and your pension will continue building up as normal based on your pensionable earnings at the date you went on leave.\n\nUnpaid leave:\nDuring unpaid leave, your contributions will stop and you will normally stop building up pension benefits. On your return to work, you have a one-off choice to buyback your missing pension. If you choose not to, you will not have pension benefits for that period. The cost will be provided at the time.\n\nIf you elect to buyback, you can pay monthly over a maximum 6 month period or as a one-off payment from salary.\n\nIf you die:\nIf you die while on maternity, paternity, adoption or parental leave, the same death benefits are payable as for death in pensionable service, whether the leave is paid or unpaid.\"\n        keywords = \"maternity,paternity,adoption,parental leave,buyback\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - What happens to my pension if I am absent due to illness?\"\n        content = \"Paid sick leave:\nDuring paid sick leave, your pension will build up based on the pay you actually receive during the period of absence.\n\nUnpaid sick leave:\nDuring unpaid sick leave, your contributions will stop and you will stop building up pension. There is no facility to make up contributions when you return to work.\n\nIf you die:\nIf you die while on sick leave, the same death benefits are payable as for death in pensionable service, whether the leave is paid or unpaid. If you die while on unpaid leave, the life cover lump sum and prospective pension will generally be based on your pensionable earnings at the date you went on leave.\"\n        keywords = \"sick leave,illness,absence,contributions\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - What if my service record is incorrect?\"\n        content = \"The Pension Fund is advised of your Company and Pensionable start date by the Company.\n\nIf you joined a Unilever Company before 1988, you were unable to join the Fund until age 21. The user wants me to:
1. Extract Q&A pairs from the FAQ document
2. Create knowledge articles in their Dynamics 365 Customer Service environment
3. Publish each knowledge article

Looking at the FAQ, I can identify numerous question-answer pairs. I need to use the Dynamics 365 API to create knowledge articles. Based on the copilot-instructions.md, the Dynamics 365 environment is:
- Environment URL: https://org6cb3e9fb.crm4.dynamics.com
- API Base: https://org6cb3e9fb.crm4.dynamics.com/api/data/v9.2/

I'll need to:
1. First, understand the knowledge article entity structure in Dynamics 365
2. Create each knowledge article using the API
3. Publish each article

Let me start by checking if there's an MCP server for Dataverse that I can use, or I'll need to use PowerShell/REST API calls.

Looking at the workspace, there's an `mcp-dataverse-server` folder which suggests there might be a Dataverse MCP server available. However, I don't see any Dataverse-specific tools in my available tools list.

I'll need to use the terminal to make REST API calls to Dynamics 365. First, let me get an access token and then create the knowledge articles.

The knowledge article entity in Dynamics 365 is `knowledgearticles`. Key fields include:
- title
- content (HTML or plain text)
- keywords
- description
- statecode/statuscode for publishing

Let me start by identifying the Q&A pairs and then creating the articles.

From the FAQ, here are the Q&A pairs I can identify:

Section 2 - Membership:
1. Q: How do I join the fund? A: The DB section closed 30 Sept 2021, new employees enrolled in RSP via Fidelity...
2. Q: I recently joined but haven't received a new joiner pack? A: If joined after 30 Sept 2021, they're RSP members...


3. Q: How much do I contribute? A: 5% of pensionable earnings up to upper limit (£45,000)...
4. Q: What is the Benefits Envelope? A: 25% of gross pensionable earnings...
5. Q: Can I make additional contributions? A: Yes, EVCs to Investing plan...
6. Q: Will I receive tax relief on contributions? A: Yes, at highest rate of tax...
7. Q: My contributions/balance are less than expected - why? A: Check if looking at Fidelity/SMPI statement...
8. Q: What is the limit on contributions? A: Normally...

The contribution limit extends to 40 years, with the possibility to extend further to 45. I can transfer benefits into the Investing plan if both Unilever and the Trustees approve. There are restrictions on transferring out—I need to apply at least 6 months before my Normal Retirement Age. I'm able to opt out by downloading a form from uukpf.co.uk. When I leave the scheme, what happens depends on how long I've been a member. Pension increases during deferment follow different rates depending on the period. If I move to part-time work, my contributions adjust accordingly. Maternity and paternity leave treatment varies based on whether the leave is paid or unpaid, and sick leave has different implications depending on whether it's paid.

If my service record contains errors, the Fund relies on information provided by the Company. International assignees who localize in the UK after September 30, 2021 are enrolled in the RSP. Transferring overseas depends on the type of assignment I'm on. For death benefits, my spouse or civil partner receives a pension if I pass away. To find out the current value of a spouse's pension, I need to open a case rather than requesting quotes over the phone. Before retirement, I may have options to increase the spouse pension. Children receive pensions up to age 18 or 23 depending on circumstances, and determining who qualifies as a dependant follows specific eligibility criteria.

A lump sum is payable on death with amounts varying by membership status. To designate who receives this lump sum, I complete a nomination form with sections for different beneficiary categories. Additional life cover can be purchased up to 8 times my pensionable earnings. When a member dies, a P45 is issued once all payments are finalized, though a P60 isn't sent automatically. The accrual rate is 1/80 from October 1, 2021, and my pension calculation uses both Career Average and Final Salary formulas. I can request quotes and estimates for my benefits.

    "original": "# Batch 4: International Assignees and Death Benefits\n$articles = @(\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - International Assignees localising in the UK\"\n        content = \"Employees may come to the UK on an international assignment, joining the UK payroll and paying NI Contributions but staying in their home country pension fund.\n\nSome IAs do not return to their home country and are localised - meaning all assignment allowances stop, contributions to home pension fund cease, and they are treated the same as any other locally recruited UK employee.\n\nIAs who localise after 30 September 2021 and have not opted out of the UUKPF previously should be enrolled into the RSP and queries forwarded to Fidelity as appropriate.\"\n        keywords = \"international assignee,IA,localise,UK,RSP,Fidelity\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - What happens to my pension if I transfer overseas?\"\n        content = \"If going on an International Assignment and expected to return to the UK:\nContact the Expert Admin Team (EAT) who can confirm pension arrangements following transfer overseas on assignment. Email: expertadminteam@unilever.com\n\nIf moving on a permanent transfer:\nYou will be treated in the same way as a voluntary leaver.\"\n        keywords = \"overseas,international assignment,transfer,EAT\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Spouse/civil partner pension on death\"\n        content = \"A pension will be payable to a legally married spouse or civil partner on your death.\n\nIf you have been married or in a civil partnership less than six months before your death, a pension is only payable at Trustees discretion.\n\nA pension may be payable to a dependant at the Trustees discretion. Complete a dependant partner nomination form from uukpf.co.uk.\n\nIf in service:\nHalf the pension you have built up to death, plus if you die before age 65, half the pension you could have built up from death to age 65 (up to maximum pensionable service) based on pensionable earnings at death up to the upper limit.\n\nIf deferred:\nHalf your deferred pension, including increases up to date of death. If left before 06/04/1997, your automatic lump sum will be converted into pension for your spouse/civil partner.\n\nIf retired:\nHalf the pension you were receiving at death (ignoring any reduction from taking a cash sum).\n\nThe pension will be adjusted if your spouse/civil partner is more than 10 years older or younger than you.\"\n        keywords = \"spouse,civil partner,death,pension,survivor\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Can I increase pension payable to my spouse/civil partner?\"\n        content = \"Before you retire, you may be able to choose to start with a smaller pension for yourself and increase the amount payable to your spouse or civil partner after you die (up to a certain maximum).\n\nIf you wish to investigate this option, please confirm your spouse or civil partners date of birth and Capita will refer to the actuary for calculation.\"\n        keywords = \"spouse pension,increase,civil partner,actuary\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Childrens pensions on death\"\n        content = \"Pensions are payable to eligible children up to age 18 (or 23 if in full-time education) in the event of your death.\n\nChildrens pensions are worked out as a percentage of your pension, depending on whether a spouse/partner pension is also payable and how many children are entitled:\n\nNumber of Children: 1, 2, 3, 4 or more\nIf spouse/partner pension paid: 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%\nIf no other pension paid: 30%, 45%, 60%, 75%\n\nThe total is shared equally among eligible children.\n\nA childs pension stops at age 18 (or 23 if still in full-time education). If a child is severely disabled, the Trustees may decide to pay them a pension for life.\"\n        keywords = \"children,pension,death,dependant,education\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - How is eligibility for dependant pension determined?\"\n        content = \"Upon your death, Capita will issue the informant with a beneficiary information form to identify any potential beneficiaries.\n\nAny dependant pension applications should be declared, and relevant evidence of financial dependency provided.\n\nIf there is a completed dependant partner nomination form on record in the name of the applicant and the Trustees have accepted this previously, the pension will be put into payment.\n\nIf there is no form on record, the information will be forwarded to the Trustees for them to assess the applicants eligibility for a pension.\"\n        keywords = \"dependant,eligibility,pension,nomination,trustees\"\n    }\n)\n\n$createdCount = 0\nforeach ($article in $articles) {\n    $body = @{\n        title = $article.title\n        content = $article.content\n        keywords = $article.keywords\n        description = $article.title\n    } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10\n\n    try {\n        $result = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles\" -Headers $global:headers -Method Post -Body $body\n        Write-Host \"Created: $($article.title)\"\n        $createdCount++\n    } catch {\n        Write-Host \"Failed: $($article.title) - $($_.Exception.Message)\"\n    }\n}\nWrite-Host \"&#96;nBatch 4 complete: $createdCount articles created\""

Payable as long as you are a Unilever employee - you do not have to be building up benefits in a pension fund\n- Any extra life cover you have arranged from the plan\n- A refund of member contributions with interest (not including contributions towards extra life cover, serious ill health cover or Benefits Envelope paid by Unilever)\n- The value of your Investing plan account (normally payable as a cash sum)\n\nIf deferred:\n- A refund of member contributions with interest\n- The value of your Investing plan account (normally payable as a cash sum)\n\nIf retired:\nIf you die within five years of retiring, the balance of your pension for the rest of that five-year period (based on the monthly rate at death) will be payable as a cash sum.\n\nNote: GMP and EPB only members do not have a Lump Sum payment payable upon death.\"\n        keywords = \"death,lump sum,life cover,refund,cash sum\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - How to nominate beneficiaries for death lump sum\"\n        content = \"Complete a nomination form to guide the Trustees about who should receive any cash sum benefit if you die. {
  "kind": "terminal",
  "terminalToolSessionId": "717a84c4-28a8-467d-a31c-33892aa1f38e",
  "terminalCommandId": "tool-f5060218-2818-44f3-937d-8899720b6b55",
  "commandLine": {
    "original": "# Batch 6: Benefits - Calculations, Quotes, Transfers\n$articles = @(\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - What is the pension accrual rate?\"\n        content = \"From 1 October 2021, the accrual rate for future CARE pension entitlement is 1/80.\"\n        keywords = \"accrual rate,1/80,CARE,pension\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - How is my pension calculated?\"\n        content = \"Career Average Plan:\nYou earn a yearly pension of 1/80 of your pensionable earnings up to the upper limit for each year of pensionable service (adjusted if you join or leave part way through a year). This yearly amount then increases each year in line with inflation up to a maximum of 5% until you leave pensionable service.\n\nYour total CARE pension on leaving the scheme is each years accrued pension (plus increases) added together.\n\nFinal Salary Plan:\nThe higher of:\n(1) 1/60 of your final pensionable salary at date of leaving multiplied by your pensionable service up to 30 June 2012 (calculated in years and months)\n(2) Your Final Salary Pension calculated at 30 June 2012 (using the methodology above) with pension increases applied to date of leaving.\n\nFor a full breakdown or further clarification, please contact Capita to open a case.\"\n        keywords = \"pension calculation,CARE,final salary,1/60,1/80\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Can I get a quote or estimate of my pension?\"\n        content = \"Yes! You can request a pension quote or estimate by contacting Capita.\n\nPlease note: We should only offer a maximum of 3 quotes and there is little point doing quotes for retirement dates quite close to each other (e.g. doing quotes for both May and June 2022).\"\n        keywords = \"quote,estimate,pension,retirement\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Can I transfer my pension out of the Fund?\"\n        content = \"As long as you are a deferred member, you can request to transfer all or part of your benefits out of the Fund up to 6 months before your NPA, with transfers completed and paid before you actually reach NPA.\n\nIf you want a Cash Equivalent Transfer Value (CETV) and discharge forms, please contact Capita.\n\nYou are entitled to one free CETV in a 12 month period. Any subsequent requests are subject to a charge of 78 GBP plus VAT.\n\nPlease note: If your transfer contains DB benefits and the value is over 30,000 GBP, you will be required to seek Financial Advice and provide a statement from an FCA regulated adviser before a transfer can proceed.\n\nDB transfers are guaranteed for 3 months.\"\n        keywords = \"transfer out,CETV,deferred,financial advice\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - What is Stronger Nudge?\"\n        content = \"From 1 June 2022, Pension Schemes that provide flexible benefits (i.e. DC benefits) are required to give members a Stronger Nudge towards pension guidance delivered by PensionWise before they access or transfer benefits.\n\nIf any of your benefits contains a DC element (for example, the Investing Plan), you will be affected.\n\nAt the point of accessing or transferring your benefits, you will either be required to take the guidance from PensionWise, opt out or declare that you are exempt.\n\nIf you wish to take PensionWise guidance, you can book the appointment yourself or Capita can do this on your behalf. Your retirement or transfer request will then be placed on hold until the appointment has taken place.\"\n        keywords = \"Stronger Nudge,PensionWise,DC,guidance,transfer\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Stronger Nudge exemptions\"\n        content = \"The following transactions are exempt from Stronger Nudge:\n\nTransfer Cases:\n- Member is under age 50 (because the service is only available for people 50 and over)\n- The purpose is not to receive flexible benefits as a result of the transfer\n- Member has already been referred to guidance by another scheme (regardless of whether guidance was taken or opted out)\n- Transfer is from an occupational scheme to a personal pension scheme regulated by the FCA (receiving provider would be responsible for making the nudge)\n- A personal pension provider has already provided retirement risk warnings and circumstances have not changed significantly\n\nRetirement Cases:\n- Received Pension Wise guidance in the last 12 months\n- Received regulated financial advice in the last 12 months\n\nThe member will need to indicate this within their Retirement Option Form.\"\n        keywords = \"Stronger Nudge,exempt,exemption,PensionWise\"\n    }\n)\n\n$createdCount = 0\nforeach ($article in $articles) {\n    $body = @{\n        title = $article.title\n        content = $article.content\n        keywords = $article.keywords\n        description = $article.title\n    } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10\n\n    try {\n        $result = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles\" -Headers $global:headers -Method Post -Body $body\n        Write-Host \"Created: $($article.title)\"\n        $createdCount++\n    } catch {\n        Write-Host \"Failed: $($article.title) - $($_.Exception.Message)\"\n    }\n}\nWrite-Host \"&#96;nBatch 6 complete: $createdCount articles created\""

{
  "kind": "terminal",
