  "commandLine": {
    "original": "# Batch 7: GMP, Retirement\n$articles = @(\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Transfer discharge forms - what next?\"\n        content = \"Transferring your pension can sometimes be a lengthy process. Even once paperwork is complete, there are multiple reasons for hold ups:\n\n- Due diligence checks - The Trustees are currently conducting enhanced due diligence checks due to changes in Pension Transfer Regulations on 30 November 2021. You may receive a letter requesting further information.\n- Awaiting dealing dates for disinvestment of DC funds.\n\nUnder legislation, Capita have 6 months from the guarantee date (the calculation date) of the CETV to pay the transfer. If the transfer application is comprised solely of DC benefits, we have 6 months from the date the transfer documentation was returned.\"\n        keywords = \"transfer,discharge,CETV,due diligence\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - What is GMP?\"\n        content = \"Until 6 April 2016, the Fund was contracted out of the State Second Pension.\n\nIf you have pensionable service between 6 April 1978 and 5 April 1997, you paid a lower rate of National Insurance contributions. In return, the UUKPF will provide you with a level of benefits equivalent to what you would have received from the State Earnings Related Pension Scheme (SERPS) had the fund not been contracted out.\n\nOnce you reach your GMP age (65 for men and 60 for women), the GMP part of your pension takes effect and receives different increases. If you are the husband, wife or civil partner of a member and receiving a pension with GMP (a widows GMP), this different increase will apply whatever your age.\"\n        keywords = \"GMP,guaranteed minimum pension,contracted out,SERPS\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Is the Fund equalised?\"\n        content = \"Benefits in the Fund are equalised with the exception of GMP.\n\nIn relation to GMP equalisation, the Trustees are currently discussing this, however there is no timescale for an update.\"\n        keywords = \"equalised,GMP,equalisation\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - What is my Normal Pension Age (NPA/NRD)?\"\n        content = \"Typically this is age 65. However there are exceptions:\n\n- Some members have a True NRA of age 60 (e.g. female GMPONLY members)\n- Some members have benefits that are payable unreduced from age 60 although their NRA is still age 65 under the Trust Deed and Rules\n- Active members and EDEF members still in relevant employment can retire after age 65 (i.e. when employment ends)\"\n        keywords = \"NPA,NRD,normal retirement,age 65,retirement age\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - to take account of the expectation that you will receive it for longer than if you had started at your NPA.\n\nThis reduction is currently 4.5% for each year you retire before NPA.\n\nIf different tranches of pension benefit are payable unreduced at different dates, each tranche will be reduced by the relevant early retirement factor accordingly.\"\n        keywords = \"early retirement,age 55,reduction,4.5%\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Ill health retirement criteria\"\n        content = \"Members must be:\n- Over age 23\n- Have 5+ years pensionable service\n- Unfit to carry out their own occupation, or have limited their earnings capacity\n\nThe case is referred to Occupational Health who then assess the members application.\"\n        keywords = \"ill health,retirement,criteria,occupational health\"\n    }\n)\n\n$createdCount = 0\nforeach ($article in $articles) {\n    $body = @{\n        title = $article.title\n        content = $article.content\n        keywords = $article.keywords\n        description = $article.title\n    } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10\n\n    try {\n        $result = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles\" -Headers $global:headers -Method Post -Body $body\n        Write-Host \"Created: $($article.title)\"\n        $createdCount++\n    } catch {\n        Write-Host \"Failed: $($article.title) - {

  "terminalCommandId": "tool-c5e2987d-3d9a-4099-ac74-d03fa43ee51e",
  "commandLine": {
    "original": "# Batch 8: More Retirement\n$articles = @(\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Ill health pension (active member)\"\n        content = \"If you have to stop working for Unilever and leave pensionable service because of serious ill health or permanent incapacity, you may be eligible to receive a pension provided you meet the criteria.\n\nThe serious ill-health pension is made up of:\n- Your Career average plan pension, based on the years worth of pension you have built up to the time you retire, plus\n- 1/80th of your pensionable earnings (up to the upper limit) for each year you could have built up pension from the time you retire to age 65. The years of pension you have built up plus these extra years are limited to your maximum pensionable service.\n\nFrom 1 October 2021, if your pensionable earnings are above the upper limit (currently 45,000 GBP) and you opted to pay for the voluntary serious ill health DC top up benefit, you may receive an additional payment from Unilever to your DCIP account. This must be used on retirement to buy additional benefits.\"\n        keywords = \"ill health,pension,active member,serious ill health\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Ill health retirement from deferred status\"\n        content = \"If you wish to apply for ill health retirement from deferred status, please contact Capita.\n\nYou will be forwarded a pack for you/your GP or consultant to complete. This will then be forwarded to Occupational Health and Unilever for them to assess your application.\n\nIf an application is approved, you will receive a pension (of which the final salary element is payable unreduced).\n\nNote: If your health improves, Unilever has the right to suspend or reduce any pension you are receiving.\"\n        keywords = \"ill health,deferred,retirement,GP,occupational health\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Retirement process\"\n        content = \"Active member:\nCapita will receive confirmation from UniOps that you are leaving your Unilever employment and are retiring. Once this notification is received, a retirement pack will be issued containing your retirement options and forms to complete.\n\nDeferred member:\nCapita will write to you approximately 13 months before your NRD with a retirement pack containing your retirement options and forms. Alternatively, contact us anytime after age 55 requesting a retirement pack.\n\nPlease keep Capita updated with any changes to your contact details.\n\nIf you do not claim benefits at NRD in a timely manner, the same level of pension as would have been payable at NRD will be paid at actual retirement and arrears will be paid. There are restrictions to the number of years of arrears (6 years, any more is at Trustees discretion), and there is normally no interest for late payment.\n\nCommon reasons for delays after returning paperwork:\n- Missing information or data mismatches\n- A transfer of benefits selected\n- Open Market Option\n- Awaiting payment of final contributions (active members only)\n- Awaiting disinvestment of Investing Plan/AVC funds\"\n        keywords = \"retirement,process,active,deferred,retirement pack\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Can I take a lump sum at retirement?\"\n        content = \"There are multiple ways to take a lump sum at retirement:\n\n- Tax free Pension Commencement Lump Sum (PCLS): Normally payable by exchanging some of your annual pension for tax free cash, up to a maximum of 25% of your total benefits. Note: There are exceptions - some members with restricted pensions due to GMP or GMPONLY members cannot commute pension into a PCLS.\n\n- Uncrystallised Pension Funds Lump Sum (UFPLS): If you have DC benefits, you can elect to take these as a UFPLS. 25% will be payable tax free and the remainder is taxable through PAYE.\n\n- Trivial Commutation Lump Sum/Small Lump Sum: For members with sufficiently small benefits (see separate article).\n\nOther providers may offer additional options (e.g. Flexible Access Drawdown). Capita recommend seeking Financial Advice before making a decision.\"\n        keywords = \"lump sum,PCLS,UFPLS,tax free,retirement\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Can I take my whole fund as a lump sum?\"\n        content = \"Members with sufficiently small benefits may be able to take the entirety of their benefits as a lump sum.\n\nTrivial Commutation Lump Sum:\nIf the HMRC valuation of your benefits in the UUKPF and elsewhere do not exceed 30,000 GBP, you may be eligible.\n\nSmall Lump Sum:\nIf the value of the Lump Sum payable (i.e. your CETV) does not exceed 10,000 GBP, this is classed as a small lump sum. These are payable regardless of benefits in payment from other schemes.\n\nNote: Currently, members with Post 17/05/1990 GMP cannot take a Trivial Commutation/Small Lump Sum.\n\nPlease contact Capita to investigate eligibility.\"\n        keywords = \"trivial commutation,small lump sum,whole fund,10000,30000\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - How does my pension increase once in payment?\"\n        content = \"Once in payment, your pension increases on 1 April each year. Different parts may receive different increases:\n\nPension built up before 1 January 2008: In line with January RPI, capped at 5%\nPension built up from 1 January 2008 - 30 June 2012: In line with January RPI, capped at 3%/5% (if paid higher rate contributions)\nPension built up from 1 July 2012 - 30 September 2021: In line with January RPI, capped at 3%/5% (if paid higher rate contributions)\nPension built up from 1 October 2021: In line with January CPI, capped at 3%\n\nIf you are at/over GMP age, the GMP element of your pension will increase as follows:\n- Pre 88 GMP receives no increases from the fund\n- Post 88 GMP receives statutory increases (September CPI capped at 3%)\n\nFor benefits from 1 January 2008 - 30 September 2021, members had the option of paying higher rate contributions to receive a higher cap on their pension increase.\"\n        keywords = \"pension increase,payment,RPI,CPI,GMP,annual increase\"\n    }\n)\n\n$createdCount = 0\nforeach ($article in $articles) {\n    $body = @{\n        title = $article.title\n        content = $article.content\n        keywords = $article.keywords\n        description = $article.title\n    } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10\n\n    try {\n        $result = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles\" -Headers $global:headers -Method Post -Body $body\n        Write-Host \"Created: $($article.title)\"\n        $createdCount++\n    } catch {\n        Write-Host \"Failed: $($article.title) - $($_.Exception.Message)\"\n    }\n}\nWrite-Host \"&#96;nBatch 8 complete: $createdCount articles created\""

  "commandLine": {
    "original": "# Batch 9: Level Pension, DC, Tax and Pay\n$articles = @(\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - What is the Level Pension Option?\"\n        content = \"The Level Pension Option can be investigated for all members with Final Salary benefits. Request this when asking for a quote or retirement pack.\n\nBy taking the Level Pension Option, you will receive a higher amount of pension when you retire, up to the Basic State Pension amount.\n\nWhen you reach State Pension Age (currently age 66+), your UUKPF pension will then decrease when you start receiving your State Pension. This effectively results in the overall amount of benefit you receive to be constant (i.e. levelled out).\"\n        keywords = \"level pension,state pension,levelled out,final salary\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Will my pension decrease at State Pension Age?\"\n        content = \"If you took the Level Pension Option at retirement, the temporary pension element will cease when you reach State Pension Age.\n\nIf you are within a month of your State Pension Age, or have passed your State Pension Age and the temporary pension has not been ceased, please contact Capita so the benefits can be reduced accordingly.\n\nTo check your State Pension Age, visit www.gov.uk/state-pension-age\"\n        keywords = \"state pension age,decrease,temporary pension,level pension\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Can I take part of my DC benefits as a lump sum and reinvest the rest?\"\n        content = \"Yes - but not with the UUKPF!\n\nAt retirement, you will have the option to take part of your benefits from the Fund and transfer the remainder elsewhere. This can be either to an external provider or a Master Trust administered by Fidelity.\"\n        keywords = \"DC,lump sum,reinvest,transfer,Fidelity\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Will I receive regular pension updates?\"\n        content = \"Active members will receive a benefit statement annually.\n\nIn addition, members paying into the DCIP will receive an annual SMPI (Statutory Money Purchase Illustration) statement.\n\nPension schemes under legislation do not have to provide deferred members with an annual statement, however Capita will issue a Preserved Benefit Update upon request.\"\n        keywords = \"updates,statement,benefit statement,SMPI,deferred\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Can I view my pension details online?\"\n        content = \"This is currently in development but we cannot give a timescale as to when this will be completed.\n\nWe will communicate to you when the online service is up and running.\"\n        keywords = \"online,pension details,view online\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - When will I get paid my pension?\"\n        content = \"Pensions are generally paid on or around the 7th or 21st of each month.\n\nIf the 7th or 21st falls on a weekend or a bank holiday, your pension will be paid on the first working day before this.\"\n        keywords = \"payment date,7th,21st,pay day\"\n    }\n)\n\n$createdCount = 0\nforeach ($article in $articles) {\n    $body = @{\n        title = $article.title\n        content = $article.content\n        keywords = $article.keywords\n        description = $article.title\n    } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10\n\n    try {\n        $result = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles\" -Headers $global:headers -Method Post -Body $body\n        Write-Host \"Created: $($article.title)\"\n        $createdCount++\n    } catch {\n        Write-Host \"Failed: $($article.title) - Parameters:

```json
{
  "kind": "terminal",
  "terminalToolSessionId": "e3fd7437-7d54-4b62-895d-63c8bed8ed6a",
  "terminalCommandId": "tool-398a14f5-bb6c-4258-a880-90210663ea7b",
  "commandLine": {
    "original": "# Batch 10: Tax - Payslips, Tax, Annual Allowance, Lifetime Allowance\n$articles = @(\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Will I get a payslip?\"\n        content = \"You will receive a payslip if your pension changes by more than 1 GBP when compared to the previous month.\n\nExceptions:\n- The March payslip which will include P60 information and so will be issued to all members\n- The April payslip for those members whose pension is increased\n\nA member can request that a payslip is sent every month.\"\n        keywords = \"payslip,pay slip,monthly,P60\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Do I pay tax on my pension?\"\n        content = \"Payment of a regular pension is subject to income tax and is therefore taxed as appropriate through PAYE.\n\nPension Commencement Lump Sums are normally paid tax free.\n\nTrivial Commutation Lump Sums and UFPLS payments are payable at a rate of 25% tax free, 75% taxable through PAYE.\"\n        keywords = \"tax,PAYE,pension,income tax,tax free\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - What is the Annual Allowance?\"\n        content = \"The Annual Allowance is the yearly amount of tax efficient pension savings you can build up in registered pension schemes before a tax charge arises (the annual allowance charge).\n\nFrom 2014/15 onwards, the Annual Allowance is 40,000 GBP.\n\nIf you are an active member, you can request an Annual Allowance statement. Alternatively, if you are at risk of exceeding the Annual Allowance, Capita will automatically issue you with a statement no later than the 6th of October following the end of the relevant tax year.\n\nThere is also a Money Purchase Annual Allowance for DC benefits which is triggered when benefits are flexibly accessed (e.g. via an UFPLS). From 2017/18 onwards, the Money Purchase Annual Allowance is 4,000 GBP. If triggered, you will be notified when UFPLS benefits are settled.\"\n        keywords = \"annual allowance,40000,tax,MPAA,money purchase\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - What is the Lifetime Allowance?\"\n        content = \"The lifetime allowance is the total amount of registered pension scheme benefits you can build up over your working life before a tax charge arises (the Lifetime Allowance charge). This includes benefits from all sources except the State Pension.\n\nThe Lifetime Allowance is 1,073,100 GBP and will remain at this level until April 2026.\n\nThe Lifetime Allowance is calculated as follows:\n\nCalculate the total benefit crystallised:\n- 20 x Annual Pension\n- PLUS any PCLS\n- PLUS any DC benefit taken\n\nCalculate the percentage:\n- Divide the total benefit crystallised by the Lifetime Allowance\n- Multiply by 100\n\nIf you are over the allowance when you retire, you will pay the Lifetime Allowance charge on the value of the benefits that exceed the Lifetime Allowance. The excess may be paid as pension or drawn as a cash sum.\"\n        keywords = \"lifetime allowance,LTA,1073100,tax charge\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Lifetime Allowance Protections (IP2016 and FP2016)\"\n        content = \"On 6th April 2016, the Standard Lifetime Allowance reduced from 1.25 million GBP to 1 million GBP. The government put LTA Protection measures in place for affected members.\n\nIndividual Protection 2016 (IP2016):\nOnly available if the value of your pension savings on 5 April 2016 was over 1 million GBP. IP2016 will give you a protected Lifetime Allowance equal to the value of your pension savings on 5 April 2016, subject to an overall maximum of 1.25 million GBP.\n\nFixed Protection 2016 (FP2016):\nAvailable to members with pension savings of any value provided they are not contributing. FP2016 will give a personal lifetime allowance of 1.25 million GBP. You must not have Enhanced Protection, Primary Protection, or any other form of Fixed Protection.\n\nFP2016 can be lost if the lifetime allowance subsequently increases to more than the protected amounts.\n\nApply online for Individual/Fixed Protection at www.gov.uk/guidance/pension-schemes-protect-your-lifetime-allowance\"\n        keywords = \"lifetime allowance,IP2016,FP2016,protection,1.25 million\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - What is A-Day?\"\n        content = \"A-Day is 6 April 2006 - it is the day the Government introduced major changes to personal and company pension rules.\n\nKey changes:\n- A new lifetime allowance was introduced, placing a limit on the amount an individual could hold in pension schemes without being taxed.\n- Most personal pensions pay out a tax-free lump sum at retirement, and this was fixed at a maximum of 25%. There is transitional protection for those who would have had the right to a higher figure based on pre-6 April 2006 rules.\n\nMembers of the Unilever UK Pension Fund are not subject to transitional protection.\"\n        keywords = \"A-Day,6 April 2006,pension rules,25%\"\n    }\n)\n\n$createdCount = 0\nforeach ($article in $articles) {\n    $body = @{\n        title = $article.title\n        content = $article.content\n        keywords = $article.keywords\n        description = $article.title\n    } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10\n\n    try {\n        $result = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles\" -Headers $global:headers -Method Post -Body $body\n        Write-Host \"Created: $($article.title)\"\n        $createdCount++\n    } catch {\n        Write-Host \"Failed: $($article.title) - $($_.Exception.Message)\"\n    }\n}\nWrite-Host \"&#96;nBatch 10 complete: $createdCount articles created\""

{

  "terminalToolSessionId": "75d527b0-1f34-4733-90e1-457a41af28dd",
  "terminalCommandId": "tool-9a353a66-c64c-4e2b-81eb-c09b800867f4",
  "commandLine": {
    "original": "# Batch 11: Divorce and Redundancy\n$articles = @(\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - What happens to my pension on divorce?\"\n        content = \"If you get divorced or end a civil partnership, your former partner will lose any automatic right to a pension if you die. However, the courts may allocate some of your pension benefits to them as part of the settlement.\n\nThe most common arrangement is transferring a specified percentage of your pension to a pension provider in your ex-spouse/civil partners name - this is known as a pension sharing order.\n\nNote: The process/requirements are different for divorce in Scotland/Northern Ireland.\n\nIf you have been separated from your husband, wife or civil partner for more than two years, you can be treated as unmarried or not in a civil partnership if you apply to the Trustees and they agree. You can then apply for a dependants pension for your new partner. If you were to die in this situation, your original spouse may still receive a reduced pension.\"\n        keywords = \"divorce,civil partnership,pension sharing order,separation\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Can I get a CETV for divorce purposes?\"\n        content = \"Yes! Capita can provide you with a Cash Equivalent Transfer Value (CETV) for divorce purposes.\n\nYou are entitled to one CETV free of charge in a 12 month period. Any additional requests will be charged at 78 GBP plus VAT.\n\nIf you are in receipt of a pension and over NPA, the CETV request is also chargeable at the above rate.\"\n        keywords = \"CETV,divorce,transfer value,78\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Pension sharing order implementation charge\"\n        content = \"The administration charge for implementing a pension sharing order is 1,350 GBP plus VAT.\n\nWho pays the administration charge is detailed in the pension sharing annex (e.g. by the member, ex-spouse/civil partner or split equally between both parties).\n\nIf applicable, the ex-spouse/civil partner can elect to have their proportion of charges deducted from their pension credit. The member can also have their charge deducted from their benefits, however this is not typically offered.\"\n        keywords = \"pension sharing order,charge,1350,divorce\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - How long does pension sharing implementation take?\"\n        content = \"Once Capita receives all information required to implement the order (including charges), Capita has 4 months under legislation to implement the order and arrange for the transfer of the pension credit. However, we will endeavour to implement the order quicker than this.\n\nProcess:\n1. Capita receives pension sharing documentation\n2. Capita reviews documents and responds to order with any required amendments and a request for ex-spouse/civil partner pension provider details within 21 calendar days (postponement of implementation)\n3. Capita issues requests for charges to relevant parties\n4. Once all information/charges received, Capita issues notice of implementation to both parties within 21 calendar days\n5. Capita then has 4 months (the implementation period) to disinvest any required DC benefits, calculate and pay the pension credit to the ex-spouse/civil partners pension provider and reduce the members benefits\n6. Capita issues notice of discharge of liability to all parties within 21 calendar days (typically done in the implementation period)\"\n        keywords = \"pension sharing,implementation,4 months,process\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - How will Capita be notified of my redundancy?\"\n        content = \"Your line manager will advise UniOps of your leaving via the Workday system. This will trigger a notification to be sent to the Unilever UK Pension Fund administrators, Capita.\"\n        keywords = \"redundancy,notification,UniOps,Workday\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Can I pay severance into my pension?\"\n        content = \"Yes, part of your severance lump sum can be paid into the DCIP.\n\nThis must be done before you leave service. You will need to speak to UniOps to arrange this.\n\nPlease note: Doing this will also count towards your Pension Input Amount for your Annual Allowance.\"\n        keywords = \"severance,lump sum,DCIP,redundancy,annual allowance\"\n    }\n)\n\n$createdCount = 0\nforeach ($article in $articles) {\n    $body = @{\n        title = $article.title\n        content = $article.content\n        keywords = $article.keywords\n        description = $article.title\n    } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10\n\n    try {\n        $result = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles\" -Headers $global:headers -Method Post -Body $body\n        Write-Host \"Created: $($article.title)\"\n        $createdCount++\n    } catch {\n        Write-Host \"Failed: $($article.title) - $($_.Exception.Message)\"\n    }\n}\nWrite-Host \"&#96;nBatch 11 complete: $createdCount articles created\""
  },

They could be about:\n\n- Am I eligible for membership of UPA?\n- Pensioner Lunches/Lunch invitations\n- Birthday cards and vouchers\n- Regional group membership\n- Visiting scheme\n- Unilever Shares\n\nPlease email expertadminteam@unilever.com or contact the Expert Admin Team on the members behalf.\"\n        keywords = \"UPA,pensioner association,shares,lunch,birthday\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - New joiners from 1 October 2021\"\n        content = \"Members who join Unilever from 1 October 2021 will be automatically enrolled into the Retirement Savings Plan (RSP) and should be forwarded to Fidelity as appropriate.\n\nExceptions handled by Capita:\n- Expression of Wish requests for RSP members\n- Death in Service for RSP/Life Assurance Only members\"\n        keywords = \"new joiner,RSP,Fidelity,1 October 2021\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF - Non-member with no pension record\"\n        content = \"If someone believes they were part of the Fund but no record exists:\n\nIf they have any paperwork or documentation to show they were part of the Fund, ask them to send a copy for investigation.\n\nPossible reasons for no record:\n- They may have been too young to join (joining was restricted to age 21+ before 1988, then 18+ from 6 April 1988)\n- Some companies had a 6 month waiting period\n- If they took a refund or transferred, a record should still exist on Hartlink or the historic transfer books\n\nIf they have evidence or know specific dates and company names, further investigation can be conducted.\"\n        keywords = \"non-member,no record,investigation\"\n    },\n    @{\n        title = \"UUKPF -     "original": "# For Knowledge Articles, the proper way to publish is:\n# 1. Create article (statecode 0/Draft)\n# 2. Approve (optional - statecode 1/Approved) \n# 3. Publish (statecode 3/Published with statuscode 7)\n\n# For archived articles (statecode 5), we need to first set them back to Draft, then Publish\n\n# Let's try using the UpdateStateValue action or direct PATCH\n$archivedArticles = $allArticles.value | Where-Object { $_.statuscode -eq 12 }\nWrite-Host \"Processing $($archivedArticles.Count) archived articles...\"\n\n$successCount = 0\n$errorSamples = @()\n\nforeach ($article in $archivedArticles) {\n    try {\n        # First set to Draft (statecode=0, statuscode=2)\n        $draftBody = @{\n            \"statecode\" = 0\n            \"statuscode\" = 2\n        } | ConvertTo-Json\n        \n        $uri = \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles($($article.knowledgearticleid))\"\n        Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Headers $global:headers -Method Patch -Body $draftBody\n        \n        # Then set to Published (statecode=3, statuscode=7)\n        $publishBody = @{\n            \"statecode\" = 3\n            \"statuscode\" = 7\n        } | ConvertTo-Json\n        \n        Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Headers $global:headers -Method Patch -Body $publishBody\n        $successCount++\n        \n        if ($successCount % 10 -eq 0) { Write-Host \"Fixed $successCount articles...\" }\n    } catch {\n        if ($errorSamples.Count -lt 3) {\n            $errorSamples += $_.Exception.Message\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nWrite-Host \"&#96;nCompleted: $successCount articles fixed\"\nif ($errorSamples.Count -gt 0) {\n    Write-Host \"Sample errors:\"\n    $errorSamples | ForEach-Object { Write-Host \"  $_\" }\n}"

This is a 502 Bad Gateway error, which is typically a server-side issue, not something the user can fix. This is happening on the Copilot/VS Code side, not related to the Dynamics 365 operations we were performing.

Let me explain what this error means and that it's not something they caused.The **502 Server Error** you're seeing is a **Copilot/GitHub service-side issue**, not something you caused or can fix on your end.

### What's happening:
- A 502 Bad Gateway error means there's a temporary problem with the Copilot backend servers
- It's unrelated to your Dynamics 365 work or the commands we ran
- These are usually transient and resolve themselves within seconds to minutes

### What you can do:
1. **Just retry** - Click in the chat and try your request again
2. **Wait a moment** - If it persists, wait 30-60 seconds and retry
3. **Check status** - Visit [githubstatus.com](https://githubstatus.com) if it keeps happening

    "original": "# Define all Q&amp;A pairs from the FAQ\n$allArticles = @(\n    # Membership Section\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - How do I join the pension fund?\"; content = \"The DB section of the UUKPF closed to new members on 30 September 2021. New employees are now automatically enrolled into the Retirement Savings Plan (RSP) which is administered by Fidelity.&#96;n&#96;nMembers who opted out of the UUKPF on 30 September 2021 will be given the opportunity to opt back into the Fund once during the next two annual election windows (normally around July/August with changes taking effect from 1 October).&#96;n&#96;nCurrent members of the UUKPF can opt out of DB and enrol in the Defined Contribution Investing Plan (DCIP) within the same employment period.\"; keywords = \"join,membership,UUKPF,pension,RSP,Fidelity,enrol\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - I haven't received my new joiner pack\"; content = \"If you joined the Company after 30 September 2021, you are a member of the Retirement Savings Plan (RSP). Please contact Fidelity for your joiner pack.&#96;n&#96;nIf you joined before 30 September 2021 and opted back into the Fund during an election window, Capita will issue a new joiner pack when notified by Unilever.\"; keywords = \"joiner pack,new member,RSP,Fidelity\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - How much do I contribute to the pension?\"; content = \"Your contributions are 5% of your pensionable earnings up to the upper limit. As of 1 October 2021, this upper limit is 45,000 GBP and will increase annually in line with inflation.&#96;n&#96;nYou can add to your benefits with Extra Voluntary Contributions (EVCs) into the DC Investing Plan. These can be regular or one-off payments.\"; keywords = \"contributions,5%,pensionable earnings,EVCs,voluntary\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What is the Benefits Envelope?\"; content = \"The Benefits Envelope is an amount of money, calculated at 25% of your gross pensionable earnings.&#96;n&#96;nIt can be used to:&#96;n- Build up future benefits in the DB CARE plan (if eligible)&#96;n- Use for savings into the DCIP&#96;n- Use for additional taxable take-home pay&#96;n&#96;nYou can decide what to do with your Benefits Envelope each year during the annual election window.\"; keywords = \"benefits envelope,25%,CARE,DCIP,election window\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - Can I make additional contributions?\"; content = \"Yes, you can pay extra voluntary contributions to an Investing plan account in order to build up additional pension for your retirement. You can pay them on a regular basis or as occasional one-off payments.&#96;n&#96;nDownload the form from the downloadable documents section on the UUKPF website www.uukpf.co.uk and return it to the Pension team. Arrangements will be made with payroll for deductions to commence.&#96;n&#96;nMembers can also elect to pay voluntary contributions during the annual election window to increase their Life Assurance Multiplier (for death in service), or top up their serious ill health benefits.\"; keywords = \"additional contributions,EVCs,voluntary contributions,investing plan\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - Will I receive tax relief on my contributions?\"; content = \"Tax relief applies to your contributions at your highest rate of tax.&#96;n&#96;nContributions are typically deducted from your salary using the Unilever Contribution Arrangement (also known as a salary sacrifice arrangement). Under the Unilever Contribution Arrangement, you will also benefit from National Insurance contribution savings in addition to the tax relief.\"; keywords = \"tax relief,contributions,salary sacrifice,NI,national insurance\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - Why are my contributions/balance less than expected?\"; content = \"If you are looking at your Fidelity Investing Plan or a Statutory Money Purchase Illustration (SMPI) statement, this relates to your DC benefits only. These will fluctuate on a daily basis in line with your chosen investment.&#96;n&#96;nIf looking at a benefit statement or annual renewal statement, remember that your contributions and your employers go towards funding your pension accrual in the CARE Plan. The figure on your statement is an annual pension payable for life - it is not a pot of money used to purchase a pension at retirement.\"; keywords = \"contributions,balance,SMPI,Fidelity,benefits,statement\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What is the limit on how long I can contribute?\"; content = \"You will normally contribute towards benefits in the Career average plan for up to 40 years. When you reach 40 years pensionable service, you have the option to continue contributions and build up further benefits for up to 45 years.&#96;n&#96;nYour maximum pensionable service will be 40 years, or if you have reached 40 years it will be 40 or 45 years, depending on the choice you made on reaching 40 years.&#96;n&#96;nIf you work part time, your pensionable service is adjusted downwards to take account of the part time hours you actually worked.\"; keywords = \"contribution limit,40 years,45 years,pensionable service,part time\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - Can I transfer in benefits from other pension schemes?\"; content = \"If you have benefits in another registered pension arrangement, you may be able to transfer them into the Investing plan, as long as Unilever and the Trustees agree and the benefits do not include any contracted-out benefits.&#96;n&#96;nTransfers in are now managed by Fidelity. When Capita receives an initial request for a transfer in, it will be forwarded to Fidelity as appropriate.\"; keywords = \"transfer in,benefits,Fidelity,pension,contracted-out\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - Restrictions on transferring out within 6 months of NRA\"; content = \"Under their current discretionary policy, the Company and the Trustees have agreed that you must apply to transfer at least 6 months before your normal retirement age. All transfer requirements must be completed and the transfer paid before normal retirement age.&#96;n&#96;nThis current policy gives you more time than your statutory right which requires you to apply and confirm the decision to transfer more than a year before your Normal Pension Age.\"; keywords = \"transfer out,NRA,6 months,retirement,restrictions\" }\n)\n\nWrite-Host \"Prepared $($allArticles.Count) articles for batch 1...\""

  "commandLine": {
    "original": "# Create articles with isrootarticle = false, then publish them\n$createdIds = @()\n\nforeach ($article in $allArticles) {\n    $body = @{\n        title = $article.title\n        content = $article.content\n        keywords = $article.keywords\n        description = $article.title\n        isrootarticle = $false\n    } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10\n\n    try {\n        $result = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles\" -Headers $global:headers -Method Post -Body $body\n        $createdIds += $result.knowledgearticleid\n    } catch {\n        Write-Host \"Failed to create: $($article.title)\"\n    }\n}\n\nWrite-Host \"Created $($createdIds.Count) articles in batch 1\"\n\n# Now publish them (set statecode=3, statuscode=7)\n$publishedCount = 0\nforeach ($id in $createdIds) {\n    try {\n        $publishBody = @{\n            statecode = 3\n            statuscode = 7\n        } | ConvertTo-Json\n        \n        $uri = \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles($id)\"\n        Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Headers $global:headers -Method Patch -Body $publishBody\n        $publishedCount++\n    } catch {\n        Write-Host \"Failed to publish article $id\"\n    }\n}\n\nWrite-Host \"Published $publishedCount articles from batch 1\""

    "original": "# Check how many were created and their current state\nWrite-Host \"Created IDs count: $($createdIds.Count)\"\n\n# Check the current state of one article\nif ($createdIds.Count -gt 0) {\n    $testArticle = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles($($createdIds[0]))?&#96;$select=title,statecode,statuscode,isrootarticle\" -Headers $global:headers -Method Get\n    Write-Host \"Test article state:\"\n    Write-Host \"  Title: $($testArticle.title)\"\n    Write-Host \"  statecode: $($testArticle.statecode)\"\n    Write-Host \"  statuscode: $($testArticle.statuscode)\"\n    Write-Host \"  isrootarticle: $($testArticle.isrootarticle)\"\n}\n\n# Try publishing with a single article to see the error\ntry {\n    $publishBody = @{ statecode = 3; statuscode = 7 } | ConvertTo-Json\n    $uri = \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles($($createdIds[0]))\"\n    Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Headers $global:headers -Method Patch -Body $publishBody\n    Write-Host \"Published successfully!\"\n} catch {\n    Write-Host \"Publish error: $($_.Exception.Message)\"\n    # Get more details from the response\n    $reader = New-Object System.IO.StreamReader($_.Exception.Response.GetResponseStream())\n    $reader.BaseStream.Position = 0\n    $errorBody = $reader.ReadToEnd()\n    Write-Host \"Error details: $errorBody\"\n}"

{
  "kind": "terminal",

  "terminalCommandId": "tool-c8834cdd-170a-4943-b74b-1c06d0ce96b4",
  "commandLine": {
    "original": "# Get all non-root UUKPF articles (these are the ones we want to publish)\n$articlesToPublish = $newArticles.value | Where-Object { $_.isrootarticle -eq $false }\nWrite-Host \"Articles to publish (isrootarticle=False): $($articlesToPublish.Count)\"\n\n# Use SetStateRequest bound action to change state\n$publishedCount = 0\n$errors = @()\n\nforeach ($article in $articlesToPublish) {\n    try {\n        # Use the SetState action\n        $setStateBody = @{\n            \"EntityMoniker\" = @{\n                \"@odata.type\" = \"Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.knowledgearticle\"\n                \"knowledgearticleid\" = $article.knowledgearticleid\n            }\n            \"State\" = 3  # Published\n            \"Status\" = 7  # Published\n        } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10\n        \n        $uri = \"$global:baseUrl/SetState\"\n        $result = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Headers $global:headers -Method Post -Body $setStateBody\n        $publishedCount++\n    } catch {\n        if ($errors.Count -lt 3) {\n            $errors += \"$($article.title): $($_.Exception.Message)\"\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nWrite-Host \"Published: $publishedCount\"\nWrite-Host \"Errors: $($errors.Count)\"\nif ($errors.Count -gt 0) { $errors | ForEach-Object { Write-Host \"  $_\" } }"

{
  "kind": "terminal",

  "commandLine": {
    "original": "# Try the WinOpportunity-style bound action for knowledge articles\n# The correct approach is to use the UpdateStateValue action\n\n$articlesToPublish = $newArticles.value | Where-Object { $_.isrootarticle -eq $false }\n$publishedCount = 0\n$errors = @()\n\nforeach ($article in $articlesToPublish) {\n    try {\n        # Try direct entity update with state\n        $uri = \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles($($article.knowledgearticleid))\"\n        \n        # First, let's try to update just the statecode\n        $updateBody = @{\n            \"statecode\" = 3\n            \"statuscode\" = 7\n        } | ConvertTo-Json\n        \n        $result = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Headers $global:headers -Method Patch -Body $updateBody\n        $publishedCount++\n    } catch {\n        # Get full error\n        $errMsg = $_.Exception.Message\n        try {\n            $reader = New-Object System.IO.StreamReader($_.Exception.Response.GetResponseStream())\n            $reader.BaseStream.Position = 0\n            $errDetails = $reader.ReadToEnd() | ConvertFrom-Json\n            $errMsg = $errDetails.error.message\n        } catch {}\n        \n        if ($errors.Count -lt 2) {\n            $errors += $errMsg\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nWrite-Host \"Published: $publishedCount out of $($articlesToPublish.Count)\"\nif ($errors.Count -gt 0) { \n    Write-Host \"Sample errors:\"\n    $errors | ForEach-Object { Write-Host \"  $_\" } \n}"

{
  "kind": "terminal",
  "terminalToolSessionId": "edd357eb-eae0-4f28-a321-094cbbb72651",
  "terminalCommandId": "tool-833c7eeb-b378-425d-95bb-0db43531f9dc",
  "commandLine": {
    "original": "# Batch 2: More FAQ articles\n$batch2 = @(\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - Can I opt out of the pension scheme?\"; content = \"Yes, you can opt out of the plan at any time. You can download a copy of the opt out form from uukpf.co.uk.&#96;n&#96;nPlease note that once opted out, you will only have one chance to opt back into the DB section of the Fund either in the next or following election window.\"; keywords = \"opt out,leave scheme,election window\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What happens if I leave the pension scheme?\"; content = \"If you have two or more years pensionable service:&#96;nYou will become a deferred member. Your benefits will be calculated at the date you left and effectively frozen until you elect to take them (from age 55). Benefits receive annual increases in deferment.&#96;n&#96;nYour Investing plan account continues to be invested. You cannot make further contributions but can still change fund choices.&#96;n&#96;nIf over age 55, you can retire directly from active service provided you have left relevant employment.&#96;n&#96;nIf you have less than two years pensionable service:&#96;nYou can elect to receive a refund of your contributions plus interest, plus any Investing Plan contributions plus investment growth, less tax.&#96;n&#96;nIf no reply received within 4 months, the default option is an automatic refund of contributions.\"; keywords = \"leave scheme,deferred,refund,contributions,leaving service\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - How does my pension increase in deferment?\"; content = \"Benefits accrued before 1 July 2012: In line with January RPI up to a maximum of 5%&#96;n&#96;nBenefits accrued between 1 July 2012 and 30 September 2021: By the lower of:&#96;n- The amount of RPI inflation over the whole period&#96;n- 2.5% for each year for the whole period&#96;n&#96;nBenefits accrued from 1 October 2021: By the lower of:&#96;n- The amount of CPI inflation over the whole period&#96;n- 2.5% for each year for the whole period&#96;n&#96;nIf you leave due to redundancy, company sale or outsourcing, the CARE element of your pension may be increased in the same way as if you were still in pensionable service.\"; keywords = \"deferment,increases,RPI,CPI,inflation,deferred pension\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What happens if I work part-time?\"; content = \"If you work part time, your contributions are adjusted to reflect this. They are still based on your pensionable earnings, but the lower and higher levels are reduced in line with the number of hours you actually work compared with full-time hours.\"; keywords = \"part-time,contributions,hours,adjusted\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What happens to my pension on maternity or paternity leave?\"; content = \"Paid leave:&#96;nDuring paid maternity, paternity, adoption or parental leave, you will pay contributions on the pay you receive and your pension will continue building up as normal.&#96;n&#96;nUnpaid leave:&#96;nDuring unpaid leave, your contributions will stop and you will normally stop building up pension benefits. On your return to work, you have a one-off choice to buyback your missing pension.&#96;n&#96;nIf you elect to buyback, you can pay monthly over a maximum 6 month period or as a one-off payment from salary.&#96;n&#96;nIf you die:&#96;nThe same death benefits are payable as for death in pensionable service, whether the leave is paid or unpaid.\"; keywords = \"maternity,paternity,adoption,parental leave,buyback\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What happens to my pension if I am absent due to illness?\"; content = \"Paid sick leave:&#96;nDuring paid sick leave, your pension will build up based on the pay you actually receive during the period of absence.&#96;n&#96;nUnpaid sick leave:&#96;nDuring unpaid sick leave, your contributions will stop and you will stop building up pension. There is no facility to make up contributions when you return to work.&#96;n&#96;nIf you die:&#96;nThe same death benefits are payable as for death in pensionable service, whether the leave is paid or unpaid.\"; keywords = \"sick leave,illness,absence,contributions\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What if my service record is incorrect?\"; content = \"The Pension Fund is advised of your Company and Pensionable start date by the Company.&#96;n&#96;nIf you joined a Unilever Company before 1988, you were unable to join the Fund until age 21. This reduced to age 18 from 6 April 1988. Some Unilever Companies also had a 6 month waiting period.&#96;n&#96;nIf you believe your service dates are incorrect, please contact Capita for investigation.\"; keywords = \"service record,dates,incorrect,start date\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - International Assignees localising in the UK\"; content = \"Employees may come to the UK on an international assignment, joining the UK payroll and paying NI Contributions but staying in their home country pension fund.&#96;n&#96;nSome IAs do not return to their home country and are localised - meaning all assignment allowances stop, contributions to home pension fund cease, and they are treated the same as any other locally recruited UK employee.&#96;n&#96;nIAs who localise after 30 September 2021 and have not opted out of the UUKPF previously should be enrolled into the RSP and queries forwarded to Fidelity.\"; keywords = \"international assignee,IA,localise,UK,RSP,Fidelity\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What happens to my pension if I transfer overseas?\"; content = \"If going on an International Assignment and expected to return to the UK:&#96;nContact the Expert Admin Team (EAT) who can confirm pension arrangements following transfer overseas on assignment. Email: expertadminteam@unilever.com&#96;n&#96;nIf moving on a permanent transfer:&#96;nYou will be treated in the same way as a voluntary leaver.\"; keywords = \"overseas,international assignment,transfer,EAT\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - Spouse/civil partner pension on death\"; content = \"A pension will be payable to a legally married spouse or civil partner on your death.&#96;n&#96;nIf you have been married or in a civil partnership less than six months before your death, a pension is only payable at Trustees discretion.&#96;n&#96;nIf in service:&#96;nHalf the pension you have built up to death, plus if you die before age 65, half the pension you could have built up from death to age 65.&#96;n&#96;nIf deferred:&#96;nHalf your deferred pension, including increases up to date of death.&#96;n&#96;nIf retired:&#96;nHalf the pension you were receiving at death.&#96;n&#96;nThe pension will be adjusted if your spouse/civil partner is more than 10 years older or younger than you.\"; keywords = \"spouse,civil partner,death,pension,survivor\" }\n)\n\n# Create and publish batch 2\n$createdCount = 0\n$publishedCount = 0\n\nforeach ($article in $batch2) {\n    # Create\n    $body = @{ title = $article.title; content = $article.content; keywords = $article.keywords; description = $article.title; isrootarticle = $false } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10\n    try {\n        $result = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles\" -Headers $global:headers -Method Post -Body $body\n        $createdCount++\n        \n        # Get the non-root version and publish it\n        $versions = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles?&#96;$filter=title eq '$($article.title)' and isrootarticle eq false&amp;&#96;$select=knowledgearticleid\" -Headers $global:headers -Method Get\n        if ($versions.value.Count -gt 0) {\n            $uri = \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles($($versions.value[0].knowledgearticleid))\"\n            $publishBody = @{ statecode = 3; statuscode = 7 } | ConvertTo-Json\n            Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Headers $global:headers -Method Patch -Body $publishBody\n            $publishedCount++\n        }\n    } catch {}\n}\n\nWrite-Host \"Batch 2: Created $createdCount, Published $publishedCount\""
  },
  "language": "pwsh",

{
  "kind": "terminal",
  "terminalToolSessionId": "ea956bb7-8da2-4bba-9303-664afed5c6d2",
  "terminalCommandId": "tool-a1a41a28-6480-43b5-aace-76f6585ee884",
  "commandLine": {
    "original": "# Batch 3: Death benefits and lump sums\n$batch3 = @(\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - Children's pensions on death\"; content = \"A pension will be paid to any eligible child under age 18 (or 23 if in full-time education) if you die in pensionable service, deferred or retired membership.&#96;n&#96;nAmount: Total children pension equals Spouse pension. If only one child, only half is paid. If 2+ children, they share the equivalent of the spouse pension.&#96;n&#96;nDuration: Paid until age 18 or 23 if in full-time education.&#96;n&#96;nDependent children over 18 or 23 who are permanently handicapped and dependent on the member could receive pension if they became disabled whilst eligible.\"; keywords = \"children,death,pension,education,dependent\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - Lump sum on death in service\"; content = \"A lump sum of four times Basic Pay is payable if you die in pensionable service (or four times Pensionable Pay if greater).&#96;n&#96;nThe lump sum is not automatically paid to a specific person. The Trustees decide who should receive it, considering members nominations and other circumstances. This is to avoid the lump sum forming part of your estate and being liable to inheritance tax.\"; keywords = \"death in service,lump sum,four times salary\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - Who is eligible to receive the death in service lump sum?\"; content = \"Benefits may be paid to your spouse, civil partner, children, cohabitee, family member, friend, colleague, estate, or even a charity.&#96;n&#96;nWhen benefits become payable, the Trustees consider all circumstances and exercise their discretion. If you have made a nomination, the Trustees will consider your wishes. A nomination is important and should be kept up to date.\"; keywords = \"death in service,nomination,beneficiary,lump sum\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - Lump sum on death in deferment\"; content = \"If you die after leaving Unilever and before you retire, a death benefit equal to five times your deferred annual pension is payable, subject to a minimum of 50% of the amount of your contributions.&#96;n&#96;nThe lump sum is discretionary and will be paid considering your nominations.\"; keywords = \"death in deferment,lump sum,deferred member\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What happens if my spouse/partner dies before me?\"; content = \"If your spouse dies before you there would be no pension payable to them. However:- any children's pensions will still be payable on your death, and&#96;n- a pension may be payable to a surviving cohabitee if you are still living with them at the date of your death.\"; keywords = \"spouse death,predeceased,cohabitee\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - How do I make a nomination?\"; content = \"You can express a wish about who should receive your discretionary lump sum death benefits via the member secure portal on uukpf.co.uk&#96;n&#96;nNavigate to 'Death benefit nomination' from the home page to input your nomination online.&#96;n&#96;nNominations should be reviewed regularly and updated following any changes in personal circumstances.\"; keywords = \"nomination,death benefit,secure portal\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What is a cohabitee?\"; content = \"A cohabitee is a person who has been living with a member as their partner for at least 12 months immediately preceding their death (the member not being legally married or in a civil partnership).&#96;n&#96;nOn death in pensionable service: The cohabitee receives a spouse-level pension at Trustees discretion.&#96;n&#96;nOn death after leaving service: A pension will only be paid if the member has nominated their cohabitee and they can prove financial dependency.&#96;n&#96;nNote: A cohabitee is also often referred to as an unmarried/common law spouse or partner.\"; keywords = \"cohabitee,common law,partner,unmarried spouse\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What is GMP (Guaranteed Minimum Pension)?\"; content = \"Between April 1978 and April 1997, contracting-out of SERPS (State Earnings Related Pension Scheme) was on the basis that the occupational pension scheme guaranteed a minimum level of pension. The minimum amount is called the GMP (Guaranteed Minimum Pension).&#96;n&#96;nGMP is broadly equal to the SERPS benefit you would have received had your employer not been contracted-out.&#96;n&#96;nGMP is not an additional payment. It forms part of your overall pension. You can find your GMP entitlement on your pension statement.\"; keywords = \"GMP,guaranteed minimum pension,SERPS,contracting out\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What retirement options are available?\"; content = \"Normal Retirement Age: 65&#96;n&#96;nEarly retirement: From age 55. Benefits are reduced for early payment unless you qualify for no reduction (redundancy etc.).&#96;n&#96;nLate retirement: Up to age 75. Benefits receive actuarial increase.&#96;n&#96;nFlexible/Partial retirement: Some employers support this - check with your HR department.&#96;n&#96;nCash commutation: Up to 25% of pension as tax-free cash.&#96;n&#96;nSmall pension lump sums: Trivial commutation may allow entire pension as lump sum if below de minimis limit.\"; keywords = \"retirement,early,late,flexible,options,age 55,age 65\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What if I want to retire early?\"; content = \"Early retirement: From age 55, you may take your pension early. Benefits are reduced to reflect the longer expected payment period.&#96;n&#96;nReduction factors: Approximately 4-5% per year before normal retirement age (65).&#96;n&#96;nNo reduction may apply if: Retiring due to redundancy, company sale/outsourcing, or ill health.&#96;n&#96;nNote: Your employer must agree to early retirement if you are still in service.\"; keywords = \"early retirement,reduction,age 55\" }\n)\n\n$createdCount = 0; $publishedCount = 0\n\nforeach ($article in $batch3) {\n    $body = @{ title = $article.title; content = $article.content; keywords = $article.keywords; description = $article.title; isrootarticle = $false } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10\n    try {\n        Invoke-RestMethod -Uri \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles\" -Headers $global:headers -Method Post -Body $body | Out-Null\n        $createdCount++\n        $versions = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles?&#96;$filter=title eq '$($article.title)' and isrootarticle eq false&amp;&#96;$select=knowledgearticleid\" -Headers $global:headers -Method Get\n        if ($versions.value.Count -gt 0) {\n            $uri = \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles($($versions.value[0].knowledgearticleid))\"\n            Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Headers $global:headers -Method Patch -Body (@{ statecode = 3; statuscode = 7 } | ConvertTo-Json)\n            $publishedCount++\n        }\n    } catch {}\n}\nWrite-Host \"Batch 3: Created $createdCount, Published $publishedCount\""
  },
  "language": "pwsh",
  "autoApproveInfo": {

<summary>Tool use: **run_in_terminal**</summary>


Parameters:

```json
{
  "kind": "terminal",
  "terminalToolSessionId": "cad614b8-b83b-4822-954e-9439aa6e27e4",
  "terminalCommandId": "tool-2ebe1a39-5f41-4551-a827-80d545c8cdb5",
  "commandLine": {
    "original": "# Batch 4: Ill health, pension calculations, tax\n$batch4 = @(\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - Can I retire on ill health grounds?\"; content = \"If you are too ill to continue working, you may be able to retire early on medical grounds.&#96;n&#96;nIll health pensions may be paid without reduction if you are unlikely to work again due to illness.&#96;n&#96;nThe process: You must provide medical evidence. The Trustees Medical Adviser will review and the Trustees make the final decision.&#96;n&#96;nThere are different levels of ill health pension depending on severity.\"; keywords = \"ill health,medical,early retirement,disability\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - How is my pension calculated?\"; content = \"Your pension has two parts:&#96;n&#96;n1. Final Salary section (for service up to 30 June 2012):&#96;nPension = (Final Pensionable Salary x Accrual Rate x Years of service)&#96;n&#96;n2. CARE section (for service from 1 July 2012):&#96;nEach year, a pension is calculated based on your pensionable salary that year. These annual amounts are revalued each year until retirement.&#96;n&#96;nInvesting Plan (from 1 October 2021):&#96;nContributions are invested. At retirement, you can take benefits from your investment pot.&#96;n&#96;nTotal pension = Final Salary pension + CARE pension + Investing Plan benefits\"; keywords = \"calculation,final salary,CARE,pension formula\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What is my Final Pensionable Salary?\"; content = \"Final Pensionable Salary is the highest of:&#96;n- Basic Pay in the 12 months before leaving/retiring&#96;n- Average of any 3 consecutive years Basic Pay in the last 10 years, revalued&#96;n- Total Basic Pay in the last 3 years divided by 3&#96;n&#96;nNote: Overtime, bonuses and other irregular payments are generally not included.\"; keywords = \"final pensionable salary,FPS,basic pay,calculation\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What is the accrual rate?\"; content = \"The accrual rate determines how quickly you build up pension.&#96;n&#96;nFinal Salary section (pre-July 2012):&#96;n1/60th of Final Pensionable Salary for each year of pensionable service.&#96;n&#96;nCARE section (July 2012 to September 2021):&#96;n1/75th of Pensionable Salary each year, revalued annually.&#96;n&#96;nNote: Some members who joined before certain dates may have different accrual rates.\"; keywords = \"accrual rate,1/60th,1/75th,pension build up\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - Can I take a tax-free lump sum?\"; content = \"Yes, you can exchange part of your pension for a tax-free cash lump sum at retirement.&#96;n&#96;nMaximum: Generally 25% of your total pension value.&#96;n&#96;nExchange rate: Typically around £12-15 of cash for each £1 of annual pension given up (this varies).&#96;n&#96;nNote: Taking cash will permanently reduce your annual pension. This is also known as commutation.\"; keywords = \"tax-free,lump sum,commutation,cash,25%\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What tax will I pay on my pension?\"; content = \"Your pension is treated as earned income for tax purposes.&#96;n&#96;nPAYE: Tax is deducted at source before payment under PAYE.&#96;n&#96;nTax Code: HMRC issues a tax code. If you have other income, your tax code may be adjusted.&#96;n&#96;nState Pension: When State Pension starts, your tax code will change as State Pension is also taxable.&#96;n&#96;nNote: The tax-free cash lump sum at retirement is not taxable.\"; keywords = \"tax,PAYE,tax code,income tax\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What is the Annual Allowance?\"; content = \"The Annual Allowance is the maximum amount of pension savings you can make each year with tax relief.&#96;n&#96;nCurrent limit: £60,000 (2023/24) but may be lower if you have tapered annual allowance or high income.&#96;n&#96;nExceeding the allowance: You may have to pay an Annual Allowance charge. The Fund can pay this charge on your behalf ('scheme pays') and reduce your pension accordingly.&#96;n&#96;nNote: Pension savings include your contributions and the employer contribution.\"; keywords = \"annual allowance,tax relief,scheme pays,pension savings\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What is the Lifetime Allowance?\"; content = \"The Lifetime Allowance (LTA) was the limit on total pension savings you could build up without additional tax charges.&#96;n&#96;nNote: The LTA tax charge was abolished from 6 April 2023. However, protections (Fixed Protection, Individual Protection) may still affect your benefits.&#96;n&#96;nIf you have applied for LTA protection, you should check the implications for future pension accrual.\"; keywords = \"lifetime allowance,LTA,tax,protection\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - How does divorce affect my pension?\"; content = \"On divorce, your pension is an asset that may be considered.&#96;n&#96;nPension Sharing Order: The court may order that a portion of your pension is transferred to your ex-spouse. They would receive their own pension from the Fund.&#96;n&#96;nPension Attachment Order: Part of your pension may be paid to your ex-spouse when your benefits come into payment.&#96;n&#96;nNote: If you divorce, the Fund needs a copy of the court order. Legal charges may apply.\"; keywords = \"divorce,pension sharing,attachment,court order\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What information does the Fund provide on divorce?\"; content = \"For divorce proceedings, the Fund can provide a Cash Equivalent Transfer Value (CETV) which is the current capital value of your pension rights.&#96;n&#96;nThis is used by solicitors/courts to determine how assets should be divided.&#96;n&#96;nYou or your solicitor should contact Capita to request divorce information. There may be a fee for this service.\"; keywords = \"divorce,CETV,transfer value,solicitor\" }\n)\n\n$createdCount = 0; $publishedCount = 0\n\nforeach ($article in $batch4) {\n    $body = @{ title = $article.title; content = $article.content; keywords = $article.keywords; description = $article.title; isrootarticle = $false } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10\n    try {\n        Invoke-RestMethod -Uri \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles\" -Headers $global:headers -Method Post -Body $body | Out-Null\n        $createdCount++\n        $versions = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles?&#96;$filter=title eq '$($article.title)' and isrootarticle eq false&amp;&#96;$select=knowledgearticleid\" -Headers $global:headers -Method Get\n        if ($versions.value.Count -gt 0) {\n            $uri = \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles($($versions.value[0].knowledgearticleid))\"\n            Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Headers $global:headers -Method Patch -Body (@{ statecode = 3; statuscode = 7 } | ConvertTo-Json)\n            $publishedCount++\n        }\n    } catch {}\n}\nWrite-Host \"Batch 4: Created $createdCount, Published $publishedCount\""

{
  "kind": "terminal",
  "terminalToolSessionId": "576e535f-ca86-4842-a140-8c7cbc4ec978",
  "terminalCommandId": "tool-323fd4e7-96a3-4aa6-88e0-90414a03f9ae",
  "commandLine": {
    "original": "# Batch 5: Redundancy, transfers, contact details\n$batch5 = @(\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What happens if I am made redundant?\"; content = \"If you are made redundant at age 55 or over, you may be able to take your pension immediately without reduction (subject to company and Trustee consent).&#96;n&#96;nUnder age 55: You will become a deferred member.&#96;n&#96;nCAre element: If you leave due to redundancy, the CARE element of your pension may continue to receive annual increases as if you were still in pensionable service (rather than the lower deferred increase rates).&#96;n&#96;nInvesting Plan: Your investment pot remains invested and continues to grow.\"; keywords = \"redundancy,made redundant,early retirement,no reduction\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - Can I transfer my pension?\"; content = \"Yes, you can transfer your UUKPF benefits to another registered pension scheme.&#96;n&#96;nProcess: Request a transfer value quotation from Capita. The quote is valid for 3 months. You then have time to decide whether to proceed.&#96;n&#96;nConsiderations: Transfers from Defined Benefit schemes often require financial advice. If your transfer value exceeds £30,000, you must take regulated financial advice before transferring.&#96;n&#96;nNote: Once transferred, you give up all UUKPF benefits and rely entirely on your new arrangement.\"; keywords = \"transfer,CETV,transfer value,other scheme\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - Can I transfer a pension from another scheme into UUKPF?\"; content = \"Transfer In is no longer permitted to the UUKPF Defined Benefit section.&#96;n&#96;nHowever, you may be able to transfer benefits from other schemes into the Investing Plan (DC section). Contact Fidelity for more information about transfers to the Investing Plan.\"; keywords = \"transfer in,other scheme,DC,investing plan\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - How do I contact Capita?\"; content = \"By telephone: 0345 602 9498&#96;nLines are open Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm (excluding bank holidays).&#96;n&#96;nBy email: Via the secure messaging service on uukpf.co.uk&#96;n&#96;nBy post: UUKPF, Capita, PO Box 555, Stead House, Darlington, DL1 9YT&#96;n&#96;nSecure portal: Log in at uukpf.co.uk to view your benefits, update personal details, make nominations, and send secure messages.\"; keywords = \"contact,telephone,email,Capita,address\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What is the member portal?\"; content = \"The member secure portal at uukpf.co.uk allows you to:&#96;n&#96;n- View your current and projected pension benefits&#96;n- Update your personal details and contact information&#96;n- Make or change your death benefit nominations&#96;n- Send secure messages to Capita&#96;n- Download forms and documents&#96;n- View your annual benefit statement&#96;n&#96;nTo register, you need your National Insurance number and date of birth.\"; keywords = \"portal,website,online,uukpf.co.uk,secure\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - How do I update my personal details?\"; content = \"You can update your personal details via the member secure portal at uukpf.co.uk&#96;n&#96;nThis includes:&#96;n- Address changes&#96;n- Email address&#96;n- Telephone number&#96;n- Marital status (you should also advise of marriage, civil partnership, or divorce)&#96;n- Name changes (supporting documentation may be required)&#96;n&#96;nIf you cannot access the portal, contact Capita directly.\"; keywords = \"update,personal details,address,email,telephone\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - When will I receive my annual benefit statement?\"; content = \"Annual Benefit Statements are issued each year, typically within the first half of the year for the previous year end.&#96;n&#96;nActive members: Statement shows benefits accrued and projected pension at normal retirement age.&#96;n&#96;nDeferred members: Statement shows your preserved benefits and projected pension.&#96;n&#96;nPensioners: A P60 is issued showing pension paid and tax deducted in the tax year.&#96;n&#96;nStatements are available online via the member portal.\"; keywords = \"annual statement,benefit statement,P60\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What is State Pension?\"; content = \"State Pension is a government pension payable from State Pension age.&#96;n&#96;nCurrent State Pension age: 66, increasing to 67 between 2026 and 2028.&#96;n&#96;nYour UUKPF pension is separate from and in addition to any State Pension.&#96;n&#96;nTo check your State Pension entitlement and forecast, visit gov.uk/check-state-pension&#96;n&#96;nNote: The UUKPF was contracted-out of the State scheme between 1978 and 1997, which may affect your State Pension entitlement.\"; keywords = \"state pension,government,pension age,NI\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What is a Pension Scam?\"; content = \"Pension scams are attempts by fraudsters to steal your pension savings.&#96;n&#96;nWarning signs:&#96;n- Contact out of the blue offering a free pension review&#96;n- Promises of guaranteed high returns&#96;n- Pressure to act quickly or limited-time offers&#96;n- Offers of early access to pension before age 55&#96;n- Request to transfer to an overseas scheme&#96;n&#96;nNEVER give personal or financial details to cold callers. If it sounds too good to be true, it probably is.&#96;n&#96;nIf you suspect a scam, report to Action Fraud on 0300 123 2040.\"; keywords = \"scam,fraud,warning,cold call,transfer\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - Who are the Trustees?\"; content = \"The UUKPF is managed by a Board of Trustees who are responsible for:&#96;n- Looking after the Fund and its assets&#96;n- Paying benefits correctly and on time&#96;n- Communicating with members&#96;n- Investing the Fund assets&#96;n&#96;nThe Trustees are supported by professional advisors including actuaries, investment managers, and lawyers.&#96;n&#96;nTrustee decisions are made in the best interest of all members and beneficiaries.\"; keywords = \"trustees,governance,management,responsibility\" }\n)\n\n$createdCount = 0; $publishedCount = 0\n\nforeach ($article in $batch5) {\n    $body = @{ title = $article.title; content = $article.content; keywords = $article.keywords; description = $article.title; isrootarticle = $false } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10\n    try {\n        Invoke-RestMethod -Uri \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles\" -Headers $global:headers -Method Post -Body $body | Out-Null\n        $createdCount++\n        $versions = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles?&#96;$filter=title eq '$($article.title)' and isrootarticle eq false&amp;&#96;$select=knowledgearticleid\" -Headers $global:headers -Method Get\n        if ($versions.value.Count -gt 0) {\n            $uri = \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles($($versions.value[0].knowledgearticleid))\"\n            Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Headers $global:headers -Method Patch -Body (@{ statecode = 3; statuscode = 7 } | ConvertTo-Json)\n            $publishedCount++\n        }\n    } catch {}\n}\nWrite-Host \"Batch 5: Created $createdCount, Published $publishedCount\""
  },

Parameters:

```json
{
  "kind": "terminal",
  "terminalToolSessionId": "a398df74-74de-43c3-8d8b-04e12db6b1c1",
  "terminalCommandId": "tool-b0bda1b4-ba05-45da-94e5-6e8830bde49a",
  "commandLine": {
    "original": "# Batch 6: More topics\n$batch6 = @(\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - How do I request a pension estimate?\"; content = \"You can obtain a pension estimate in several ways:&#96;n&#96;n1. Online: Log in to the member portal at uukpf.co.uk and use the projection tools.&#96;n&#96;n2. Written request: Contact Capita to request an estimate for a specific retirement date.&#96;n&#96;nNote: Estimates are for guidance only and based on current information. Actual benefits may differ.&#96;n&#96;nAllowing 2-4 weeks for Capita to process a written estimate request is advisable.\"; keywords = \"estimate,projection,quote,retirement\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - How do I start my retirement?\"; content = \"To start drawing your pension:&#96;n&#96;n1. Contact Capita at least 3 months before your intended retirement date.&#96;n&#96;n2. Capita will send retirement options documentation including an option form.&#96;n&#96;n3. Choose your options (e.g., how much tax-free cash to take).&#96;n&#96;n4. Return the completed form with any required documents (e.g., birth certificate, marriage certificate).&#96;n&#96;n5. Capita will calculate your final benefits and set up payment.&#96;n&#96;nYour first pension payment may be a combined payment covering the period from your retirement date.\"; keywords = \"start pension,retire,claim,options form\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What documents do I need to retire?\"; content = \"When claiming your pension, you may need to provide:&#96;n&#96;n- Birth certificate or passport (proof of age)&#96;n- Marriage or civil partnership certificate (if applicable)&#96;n- Decree absolute (if divorced)&#96;n- Bank details for pension payment&#96;n- P45 from your employer (if retiring directly from service)&#96;n&#96;nCapita will advise which specific documents are required when they send your retirement pack.\"; keywords = \"documents,birth certificate,marriage certificate,P45,proof\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - When will my pension be paid?\"; content = \"Pensions are paid monthly in arrears, on the last working day of each month.&#96;n&#96;nPayment method: Direct credit to your UK bank or building society account. Overseas payments may also be possible but may incur charges.&#96;n&#96;nP60: You will receive an annual P60 showing your total pension and tax deducted for the tax year.\"; keywords = \"payment,monthly,bank,arrears\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - How do my pension increases work in retirement?\"; content = \"Your pension is reviewed annually on 1 April.&#96;n&#96;nBenefits built up before 1 July 2012: Increase by January RPI, capped at 5%.&#96;n&#96;nBenefits built up from 1 July 2012 to 30 September 2021: Increase by the lower of RPI and 2.5%.&#96;n&#96;nBenefits built up from 1 October 2021: Increase by the lower of CPI and 2.5%.&#96;n&#96;nNote: The GMP portion of your pension may have different increase rules due to State pension rules.\"; keywords = \"increases,RPI,CPI,inflation,annual increase,pensioner\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What is pension bridging?\"; content = \"Pension bridging is an option that may be available if you retire before State Pension age.&#96;n&#96;nHow it works: You receive a higher pension from your Fund retirement date until State Pension age. Once your State Pension starts, your Fund pension reduces.&#96;n&#96;nPurpose: To provide a more level total income before and after State Pension age.&#96;n&#96;nNote: The total pension received over your lifetime remains approximately the same - it is a timing adjustment, not extra pension.\"; keywords = \"bridging,state pension age,level income\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What is Added Years?\"; content = \"Added Years was a historic method of purchasing additional pension.&#96;n&#96;nHow it worked: By paying extra contributions, members could buy additional years of pensionable service, increasing their final pension.&#96;n&#96;nClosed to new purchases: This option is no longer available for new purchases, but members who previously bought Added Years retain that benefit.&#96;n&#96;nIf you have Added Years, they will be included in your pension calculation.\"; keywords = \"added years,AVC,additional,purchase\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What are AVCs?\"; content = \"AVCs (Additional Voluntary Contributions) allow you to save extra for retirement on top of your main pension.&#96;n&#96;nHistoric UUKPF AVCs: If you made AVCs before a certain date, these may provide additional benefits within the Fund.&#96;n&#96;nCurrent additional savings: New additional savings are directed to the Investing Plan (DC section) managed by Fidelity.&#96;n&#96;nContact Fidelity for information about the Investing Plan at fidelitypensions.com or call their helpline.\"; keywords = \"AVC,additional voluntary,extra,Fidelity,investing plan\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What is the Investing Plan?\"; content = \"The Investing Plan is the Defined Contribution (DC) section of UUKPF.&#96;n&#96;nFrom 1 October 2021, new members join the Investing Plan rather than the Defined Benefit section.&#96;n&#96;nHow it works: Contributions are invested in funds you choose. At retirement, you can take a tax-free lump sum and use the remainder to provide income (e.g., annuity, drawdown).&#96;n&#96;nAdministration: The Investing Plan is administered by Fidelity. Contact Fidelity directly for investment choices, fund switches, and account queries.\"; keywords = \"investing plan,DC,defined contribution,Fidelity\" },\n    @{ title = \"UUKPF - What is the difference between DB and DC?\"; content = \"Defined Benefit (DB):&#96;n- Final Salary and CARE sections&#96;n- Pension based on salary and years of service&#96;n- Guaranteed lifetime income from retirement&#96;n- Investment risk borne by the Fund&#96;n&#96;nDefined Contribution (DC):&#96;n- Investing Plan section&#96;n- Pension pot based on contributions plus investment growth&#96;n- Benefits depend on fund performance&#96;n- Investment risk borne by the member&#96;n&#96;nMany members have benefits in both sections depending on their service dates.\"; keywords = \"DB,DC,defined benefit,defined contribution,difference\" }\n)\n\n$createdCount = 0; $publishedCount = 0\n\nforeach ($article in $batch6) {\n    $body = @{ title = $article.title; content = $article.content; keywords = $article.keywords; description = $article.title; isrootarticle = $false } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10\n    try {\n        Invoke-RestMethod -Uri \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles\" -Headers $global:headers -Method Post -Body $body | Out-Null\n        $createdCount++\n        $versions = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles?&#96;$filter=title eq '$($article.title)' and isrootarticle eq false&amp;&#96;$select=knowledgearticleid\" -Headers $global:headers -Method Get\n        if ($versions.value.Count -gt 0) {\n            $uri = \"$global:baseUrl/knowledgearticles($($versions.value[0].knowledgearticleid))\"\n            Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Headers $global:headers -Method Patch -Body (@{ statecode = 3; statuscode = 7 } | ConvertTo-Json)\n            $publishedCount++\n        }\n    } catch {}\n}\nWrite-Host \"Batch 6: Created $createdCount, Published $publishedCount\""
  },
